title.zh: 卷一百二十六 載記第二十六 禿髮烏孤 禿髮利鹿孤 禿髮傉檀
title.en: Volume 126 Records 26: Tufa Wugu; Tufa Lilugu; Tufa Rutan
title.raw: 卷一百二十六 載記第二十六 禿髮烏孤 禿髮利鹿孤 禿髮傉檀 Volume 126 Records 26: Tufa Wugu; Tufa Lilugu; Tufa Rutan

sentences.zh: 禿髮烏孤

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu

sentences.zh: 禿髮烏孤，河西鮮卑人也。

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu was a man of the Hexi Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu was of the Hexi Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 其先與後魏同出。

translations.literal: His ancestors issued from the same source as Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His line shared origins with Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 八世祖匹孤率其部自塞北遷於河西，其地東至麥田、牽屯，西至濕羅，南至澆河，北接大漠。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Pigu led his tribe from north of the frontier into Hexi; their land extended east to Maitian and Qianyun, west to Shiruo, south to Jiao River, and north to the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations back Pigu led the tribe from the northern frontier into Hexi, from Maitian and Qianyun in the east to Shiruo in the west, the Jiao River in the south, and the desert in the north.

sentences.zh: 匹孤卒，子壽闐立。

translations.literal: When Pigu died, his son Shoutian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Pigu died and was succeeded by his son Shoutian.

sentences.zh: 初，壽闐之在孕，母胡掖氏因寢而產於被中，鮮卑謂被為「禿髮」，因而氏焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Shoutian was in the womb, his mother Lady Huyu gave birth in her sleep upon the quilt; the Xianbei call a quilt tufa, and therefore they took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Shoutian's mother Lady Huyu bore him in her sleep on the bedding; Xianbei call bedding tufa, hence the clan name.

sentences.zh: 壽闐卒，孫樹機能立，壯果多謀略。

translations.literal: When Shoutian died, his grandson Tuyineng succeeded; he was strong, resolute, and full of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Shoutian's grandson Tuyineng succeeded—a bold, clever leader.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，殺秦州刺史胡烈于萬斛堆，敗涼州刺史蘇愉于金山，盡有涼州之地，武帝為之旰食。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era he killed Qin Governor Hu Lie at Wanhudui, defeated Liang Governor Su Yu at Jinshan, and possessed all Liang Province; Emperor Wu lost sleep over it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era he killed Qin's governor Hu Lie at Wanhudui, routed Liang's Su Yu at Jinshan, and seized all Liang Province—Emperor Wu of Jin could not eat for worry.

sentences.zh: 後為馬隆所敗，部下殺之以降。

translations.literal: Later he was defeated by Ma Long; his subordinates killed him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long defeated him; his men killed him and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 從弟務丸立。

translations.literal: His cousin Wuwang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Wuwang took his place.

sentences.zh: 死，孫推斤立。

translations.literal: He died; his grandson Tuijin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: On his death his grandson Tuijin succeeded.

sentences.zh: 死，子思復鞬立，部眾稍盛。

translations.literal: He died; his son Sifujian succeeded, and the tribe grew somewhat stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Sifujian followed; the tribe grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 烏孤即思復鞬之子也。

translations.literal: Wugu was Sifujian's son.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu was the son of Sifujian.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，務農桑，修鄰好。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, he promoted farming and silkworms and cultivated good relations with neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: On succeeding he promoted agriculture and good relations with neighbors.

sentences.zh: 呂光遣使署為假節、冠軍大將軍、河西鮮卑大都統、廣武縣侯。

translations.literal: Lü Guang sent envoys to appoint him Acting Commander, Grand General of Champions, Grand Commander of Hexi Xianbei, and Marquis of Guangwu County.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang appointed him acting commander, Grand General of Champions, commander of Hexi Xianbei, and Marquis of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 烏孤謂諸將曰：「呂氏遠來假授，當可受不？

translations.literal: Wugu said to his generals: "Lü's clan comes from afar with a false appointment—should we accept it?"
translations.idiomatic: Wugu asked his generals: "Lü offers a distant, empty title—should we accept?"

sentences.zh: 」眾咸曰：「吾士眾不少，何故屬人！

translations.literal: All said: "Our warriors are not few—why submit to another!"
translations.idiomatic: They said: "We have plenty of men—why serve another!"

sentences.zh: 」烏孤將從之，其將石真若留曰：「今本根未固，理宜隨時。

translations.literal: Wugu was about to agree when his general Shi Zhenruoliu said: "Our roots are not yet firm; reason says we must follow the times."
translations.idiomatic: Wugu nearly agreed until Shi Zhenruoliu said: "Our base is not secure—we must bide our time."

sentences.zh: 光德刑修明，境內無虞，若致死於我者，大小不敵，後雖悔之，無所及也。

translations.literal: "Lü Guang's virtue and punishments are well ordered and his realm is untroubled; if we fight to the death against him, large and small cannot match—later, though we regret it, nothing can be done."
translations.idiomatic: "Lü Guang's realm is orderly and strong; if we defy him we cannot win, and regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 不如受而遵養之，又待其釁耳。

translations.literal: "Better to accept and nurture compliance, and also wait for his opening."
translations.idiomatic: "Accept now, grow strong, and wait for his weakness."

sentences.zh: 」烏孤乃受之。

translations.literal: Wugu thereupon accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu accepted.

sentences.zh: 烏孤討乙弗、折掘二部，大破之，遣其將石亦幹築廉川堡以都之。

translations.literal: Wugu attacked the Yifu and Zhejue tribes, inflicted a great defeat, and sent his general Shi Yigan to build Lianchuan Fort as his capital.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed the Yifu and Zhejue tribes and had Shi Yigan build Lianchuan Fort as capital.

sentences.zh: 烏孤登廉川大山，泣而不言。

translations.literal: Wugu ascended the great mountain of Lianchuan, wept, and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu climbed Lianchuan's great peak, wept, and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 石亦幹進曰：「臣聞主憂臣辱，主辱臣死，大王所為不樂者，將非呂光乎！

translations.literal: Shi Yigan advanced and said: "I have heard that when the lord worries the minister is shamed, when the lord is shamed the minister dies—what you are unhappy about, is it not Lü Guang!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yigan said: "When the lord grieves the minister is shamed—is your sorrow Lü Guang?"

sentences.zh: 光年已衰老，師徒屢敗。

translations.literal: "Guang is already old in years; his armies have repeatedly been defeated."
translations.idiomatic: "Guang is old; his armies keep losing."

sentences.zh: 今我以士馬之盛，保據大川，乃可以一擊百，光何足懼也。

translations.literal: "Now with our host's strength we hold a great river—we can strike one against a hundred; what is there to fear of Guang!"
translations.idiomatic: "With our strength on this river we can beat him a hundred to one—why fear Guang!"

sentences.zh: 」烏孤曰：「光之衰老，亦吾所知。

translations.literal: Wugu said: "Guang's aging—I too know it."
translations.idiomatic: Wugu said: "I know Guang is old."

sentences.zh: 但我祖宗以德懷遠，殊俗憚威，盧陵、契汗萬里委順。

translations.literal: "But my ancestors by virtue embraced the distant; foreign peoples feared their might; Luling and Qihan submitted from ten thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet my ancestors won distant peoples by virtue; tribes submitted from afar."

sentences.zh: 及吾承業，諸部背叛，邇既乖違，遠何以附，所以泣耳。

translations.literal: "When I inherited the enterprise, the tribes rebelled; if those near have turned away, how can the far attach—therefore I weep."
translations.idiomatic: "Since I took power the tribes have rebelled; if the near forsake us, the far will not come—that is why I weep."

sentences.zh: 」其將苻渾曰：「大王何不振旅誓眾，以討其罪。

translations.literal: His general Fu Hun said: "Great King, why not rouse the army and swear the host to punish their crime."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hun said: "Great King, raise the host and punish their treason."

sentences.zh: 」烏孤從之，大破諸部。

translations.literal: Wugu followed this and inflicted a great defeat on the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu marched and crushed the rebel tribes.

sentences.zh: 呂光封烏孤廣武郡公。

translations.literal: Lü Guang enfeoffed Wugu as Duke of Guangwu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang made Wugu Duke of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 又討意雲鮮卑，大破之。

translations.literal: He again attacked the Yiyun Xianbei and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He again routed the Yiyun Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 光又遣使署烏孤征南大將軍、益州牧、左賢王。

translations.literal: Guang again sent envoys to appoint Wugu Grand General Who Conquers the South, Governor of Yi Province, and Left Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: Guang again offered Wugu Grand General Who Conquers the South, Governor of Yi, and Left Worthy King.

sentences.zh: 烏孤謂使者曰：「呂王昔以專征之威，遂有此州，不能以德柔遠，惠安黎庶。

translations.literal: Wugu said to the envoy: "King Lü in old days by sole campaign authority obtained this province yet could not by virtue soften the distant or benefit and settle the black-haired people."
translations.idiomatic: Wugu told the envoy: "King Lü won this province by force yet never ruled with virtue or cared for the people."

sentences.zh: 諸子貪淫，三甥肆暴，郡縣土崩，下無生賴。

translations.literal: His sons are greedy and licentious, three nephews wildly violent; commanderies and counties collapse and below there is no livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: His sons are greedy, his nephews violent; the commanderies crumble and the people have no livelihood.

sentences.zh: 吾安可違天下之心，受不義之爵！

translations.literal: "How can I go against the heart of all under Heaven and accept an unrighteous rank!"
translations.idiomatic: "How can I defy the world's will and take an unrighteous title!"

sentences.zh: 帝王之起，豈有常哉！

translations.literal: "The rise of emperors and kings—has it ever been constant!"
translations.idiomatic: "Emperors rise—is there a fixed rule?"

sentences.zh: 無道則滅，有德則昌，吾將順天人之望，為天下主。

translations.literal: "Without the Way one perishes; with virtue one flourishes—I shall follow the hope of Heaven and men and be lord of all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: "The wicked fall, the virtuous rise—I will follow heaven and men and rule the realm."

sentences.zh: 」留其鼓吹羽儀，謝其使而遣之。

translations.literal: He kept their drums, pipes, feather banners, and insignia, thanked the envoy, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He kept their regalia, thanked the envoy, and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 烏孤從容謂其群下曰：「隴右區區數郡地耳！

translations.literal: Wugu calmly said to his followers: "Longyou is only a few commanderies of land!"
translations.idiomatic: Wugu told his followers calmly: "Longyou is only a few commanderies!"

sentences.zh: 因其兵亂，分裂遂至十餘。

translations.literal: Because of their military disorder, division reached more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: War has split it into more than ten pieces.

sentences.zh: 乾歸擅命河南，段業阻兵張掖，虐氐假息，偷據姑臧。

translations.literal: Gangui arrogantly commands south of the Yellow River, Duan Ye blocks troops at Zhangye, the Di tyrant breathes briefly, and they steal occupation of Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui rules south of the river, Duan Ye holds Zhangye, the Di cling to power, and they seize Guzang.

sentences.zh: 吾藉父兄遣烈。

translations.literal: I rely on my father and elder brothers' legacy of fierce virtue.
translations.idiomatic: I rely on my fathers' martial legacy.

sentences.zh: 思郭清西夏。

translations.literal: I think of Guo Qing's pacification of the western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: I aspire to pacify the western lands as Guo Qing did.

sentences.zh: 兼弱攻昧，三者何先？

translations.literal: Attacking the weak and striking the dim—which comes first?"
translations.idiomatic: Attack the weak or strike the blind—which first?"

sentences.zh: 」楊統進曰：「乾歸本我所部，終必歸服。

translations.literal: Yang Tong advanced and said: "Gangui was originally of our tribe and in the end will surely submit."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tong said: "Gangui is of our tribe and will submit in time."

sentences.zh: 段業儒生，才非經世，權臣擅命，制不由已，千里伐人，糧運懸絕，且與我鄰好，許以分災共患，乘其危弊，非義舉也。

translations.literal: "Duan Ye is a Confucian scholar whose talent is not for governing the age; powerful ministers hold command and control is not from himself; to campaign a thousand li, grain transport is cut off; moreover he is friendly with us, promising to share disaster and calamity—to take advantage of his peril is not a righteous act."
translations.idiomatic: "Duan Ye is a scholar, no statesman; his ministers hold real power; a thousand-li campaign will starve; he is our ally—striking him in peril is unjust."

sentences.zh: 呂光衰老，嗣紹沖暗，二子纂、弘，雖頗有文武，而內相猜忌。

translations.literal: "Lü Guang is aged; his heir Shao is young and dim; the two sons Zuan and Hong, though somewhat civil and martial, inwardly suspect each other."
translations.idiomatic: "Lü Guang is old; his heir is young and weak; sons Zuan and Hong are capable but mistrust each other."

sentences.zh: 若天威臨之，必應鋒瓦解。

translations.literal: "If Heaven's majesty presses them, they will surely crumble at the blade's touch."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven's blow will shatter them at a touch."

sentences.zh: 宜遣車騎鎮浩亹，鎮北據廉川，乘虛迭出，多方以誤之，救右則擊其左，救左則擊其右，使纂疲於奔命，人不得安其農業。

translations.literal: "We should send the Cavalry General to garrison Haowan and the Northern Pacifier to hold Lianchuan, strike from emptiness in rotation, confuse them many ways, rescue the right then strike the left, rescue the left then strike the right, make Zuan weary with running to commands, and men unable to rest in their farming."
translations.idiomatic: "Garrison Haowan and Lianchuan, raid from many sides, strike left when they save right—wear Zuan out and ruin their harvests."

sentences.zh: 兼弱攻昧，於是乎在，不出二年，可以坐定姑臧。

translations.literal: "Attacking the weak and striking the dim lies herein; within two years Guzang can be settled while seated."
translations.idiomatic: "Thus within two years we can take Guzang without strain."

sentences.zh: 姑臧既拔，二寇不待兵戈，自然服矣。

translations.literal: "Once Guzang is taken, the two foes need no arms and will naturally submit."
translations.idiomatic: "Once Guzang falls, the others will submit without a fight."

sentences.zh: 」烏孤然之，遂陰有吞併之志。

translations.literal: Wugu approved and thereupon secretly harbored the will to swallow and merge.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu agreed and secretly planned conquest.

sentences.zh: 段業為呂纂所侵，遣利鹿孤救之。

translations.literal: Duan Ye was invaded by Lü Zuan and sent Lilugu to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye, attacked by Lü Zuan, called Lilugu to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 纂懼，燒氐池、張掖穀麥而還。

translations.literal: Zuan feared this, burned the grain of Dichi and Zhangye, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan burned the grain stores of Dichi and Zhangye and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以利鹿孤為涼州牧，鎮西平，追傉檀入錄府國事。

translations.literal: He made Lilugu Governor of Liang Province, garrisoning Xiping, and recalled Rutan to enter and record state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He made Lilugu governor at Xiping and recalled Rutan to manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 是歲，烏孤因酒墜馬傷脅，笑曰：「幾使呂光父子大喜。

translations.literal: That year Wugu, from wine, fell from his horse and injured his side; he laughed and said: "Nearly made Lü Guang and his sons greatly happy."
translations.idiomatic: That year Wugu fell drunk from his horse and hurt his ribs, laughing: "Nearly gave Lü Guang's house cause to rejoice."

sentences.zh: 」俄而患甚，顧謂群下曰：「方難未靜，宜立長君。

translations.literal: Shortly his illness grew severe; turning to his followers he said: "Square difficulties are not yet settled—we should establish a mature ruler."
translations.idiomatic: His illness worsened; he told his followers: "Trouble remains—name a mature successor."

sentences.zh: 」言終而死，在王位三年，偽諡武王，廟號烈祖。

translations.literal: When his words ended he died; he had reigned three years; his false posthumous title was King Wu, temple name Liezu.
translations.idiomatic: He died after three years' reign, posthumously titled King Wu, temple name Liezu.

sentences.zh: 弟利鹿孤立。

translations.literal: His younger brother Lilugu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Lilugu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 禿髮利鹿孤

translations.literal: Tufa Lilugu
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Lilugu

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤以隆安三年即偽位，赦其境內殊死已下，又徙居於西平。

translations.literal: Lilugu in the third year of Long'an assumed the false throne, amnestied below the death penalty within his realm, and again moved his residence to Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In Long'an year 3 Lilugu took the throne, amnestied capital crimes, and moved the capital to Xiping.

sentences.zh: 使記室監麹梁明聘于段業。

translations.literal: He sent the Recorder Qu Liangming on a mission to Duan Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Recorder Qu Liangming to visit Duan Ye.

sentences.zh: 業曰：「貴主先王創業啟運，功高先世，宜為國之太祖，有子何以不立？

translations.literal: Ye said: "Your honored master's former king founded the enterprise and opened the mandate; his merit towers above former generations—he should be the founding emperor of the state; you have a son—why not establish him?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: "Your founder's merit demands an imperial temple; you have a son—why not crown him?"

sentences.zh: 」梁明曰：「有子羌奴，先王之命也。

translations.literal: Liangming said: "There is a son, Qiangnu—it was the former king's command."
translations.idiomatic: Liangming said: "There is a son Qiangnu, as the late king commanded."

sentences.zh: 」業曰：「昔成王弱齡，周召作宰；

translations.literal: Ye said: "In old days King Cheng was young and Zhou Gong and Duke of Shao acted as ministers;"
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: "King Cheng was young yet Zhou Gong and the Duke of Shao ruled for him;"

sentences.zh: 漢昭八歲，金、霍夾輔。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhao at eight—Jin and Huo assisted on either side.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhao at eight had Jin and Huo as regents.

sentences.zh: 雖嗣子沖幼，而二叔休明，左提右挈，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: "Though the heir is young, the two uncles are bright—left hand leading, right hand supporting—is that not also possible?"
translations.idiomatic: "Though the heir is young, wise uncles can guide him—why not?"

sentences.zh: 」明曰：「宋宣能以國讓，《春秋》美之；

translations.literal: Ming said: "Duke Xuan of Song could yield the state—the Spring and Autumn Annals praised him;"
translations.idiomatic: Ming said: "Duke Xuan of Song yielded the state—the Annals praise that;"

sentences.zh: 孫伯符委事仲謀，終開有吳之業。

translations.literal: Sun Ce entrusted affairs to Sun Quan and in the end opened the enterprise of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce gave power to Sun Quan and founded Wu.

sentences.zh: 且兄終弟及，殷湯之制也，亦聖人之格言，萬代之通式，何必胤已為是，紹兄為非。

translations.literal: "Moreover elder brother ends and younger brother succeeds is the institution of Tang of Yin, also the sage's maxim and the universal pattern for ten thousand generations—why must the son be right and continuing the brother be wrong."
translations.idiomatic: "Brother succeeding brother was Tang of Yin's law—a sage's maxim for all ages—why must only sons succeed?"

sentences.zh: 」業曰：「美哉！

translations.literal: Ye said: "Beautiful!"
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 使乎之義也。」

translations.literal: The meaning of an envoy."
translations.idiomatic: That is the duty of an envoy."

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤聞呂光死，遣其將金樹、蘇翹率騎五千屯於昌松漠口。

translations.literal: Lilugu heard Lü Guang had died and sent his generals Jin Shu and Su Qiao with five thousand horse to encamp at Changsong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Lü Guang's death, Lilugu sent Jin Shu and Su Qiao with five thousand cavalry to Changsong Pass.

sentences.zh: 既逾年，赦其境內，改元曰建和。

translations.literal: When the year had passed, he amnestied his realm and changed the era to Jianhe.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he proclaimed amnesty and adopted the era Jianhe.

sentences.zh: 二千石長吏清高有惠化者，皆封亭侯、關內侯。

translations.literal: Two-thousand-bushel chief administrators who were pure and high-minded with benevolent transformation were all enfeoffed Marquis of the Hamlet or Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous governors were enfeoffed as village or within-the-passes marquises.

sentences.zh: 呂纂來伐，使傉檀距之。

translations.literal: Lü Zuan came to attack; Lilugu sent Rutan to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan attacked; Lilugu sent Rutan to meet him.

sentences.zh: 纂士卒精銳，進度三堆，三軍擾懼。

translations.literal: Zuan's soldiers were keen and sharp; advancing he crossed Sandui; the three armies were disturbed and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's elite troops crossed Sandui; Rutan's army panicked.

sentences.zh: 傉檀下馬據胡床而坐，士眾心乃始安。

translations.literal: Rutan dismounted and sat on a folding chair; the host's hearts then first settled.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan dismounted and sat on a camp stool; the troops steadied.

sentences.zh: 與纂戰，敗之，斬二千餘級。

translations.literal: He fought Zuan, defeated him, and beheaded more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Zuan and killed over two thousand.

sentences.zh: 纂西擊段業，傉檀率騎一萬，乘虛襲姑臧。

translations.literal: Zuan attacked Duan Ye in the west; Rutan led ten thousand horse, exploited the emptiness, and raided Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: While Zuan struck Duan Ye westward, Rutan raided Guzang with ten thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 纂弟緯守南北城以自固。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Wei guarded north and south cities to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's brother Wei held the inner and outer cities.

sentences.zh: 傉檀置酒於硃明門上，鳴鐘鼓以饗將士，耀兵于青陽門，虜八千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: Rutan set wine at Zhuming Gate, sounded bells and drums to feast the officers, displayed troops at Qingyang Gate, and carried off more than eight thousand households in returning.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan feasted his men at Zhuming Gate, paraded at Qingyang Gate, and carried off eight thousand households.

sentences.zh: 乞伏乾歸為姚興所敗，率騎數百來奔，處之晉興，待以上賓之禮。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui was defeated by Yao Xing and came fleeing with several hundred horse; Lilugu placed him at Jinxing and treated him with the ritual of a supreme guest.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui, beaten by Yao Xing, fled with hundreds of horse; Lilugu lodged him at Jinxing as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 乾歸遣子謙等質于西平。

translations.literal: Gangui sent his son Qian and others as hostages to Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui sent his son Qian as hostage to Xiping.

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍俱延言于利鹿孤曰：「乾歸本我之屬國，妄自尊立，理窮歸命，非有款誠；

translations.literal: The Northern Pacifier Juyan said to Lilugu: "Gangui was originally our subject state who presumptuously set himself up; his principle exhausted, he returned to allegiance—not with sincere good faith;"
translations.idiomatic: Juyan told Lilugu: "Gangui was our vassal who rebelled; his submission is not sincere;"

sentences.zh: 若奔東秦，必引師西侵，非我利也。

translations.literal: "if he flees to Eastern Qin he will surely lead troops to invade west—not to our advantage."
translations.idiomatic: "if he flees to Eastern Qin he will bring armies west—that harms us."

sentences.zh: 宜徙於乙弗之間，防其越逸之路。

translations.literal: "We should move him among the Yifu to block his path of escape."
translations.idiomatic: "Move him among the Yifu to block escape."

sentences.zh: 」利鹿孤曰：「吾方弘信義以收天下之心，乾歸投誠而徙之，四海將謂我不可以誠信託也。

translations.literal: Lilugu said: "I am just now expanding faith and righteousness to gather the hearts of all under Heaven; if Gangui comes in good faith and we move him, the four seas will say I cannot be entrusted with sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu said: "I seek to rule by faith; moving a refugee would destroy my name."

sentences.zh: 」俄而乾歸果奔于姚興。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Gangui indeed fled to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gangui fled to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤謂延曰：「不用卿言，乾歸果叛，卿為吾行也。

translations.literal: Lilugu said to Juyan: "I did not use your words—Gangui indeed rebelled; you shall go for me."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu told Juyan: "You were right—go after him."

sentences.zh: 」延追乾歸至河，不及而還。

translations.literal: Juyan pursued Gangui to the river, did not overtake him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Juyan chased Gangui to the river but failed to catch him.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤立二年，龍見於長寧，麒麟游於綏羌，於是群臣勸進，以隆安五年僭稱河西王。

translations.literal: Lilugu had reigned two years; a dragon appeared at Changning and a qilin roamed at Suiqiang; the ministers therefore urged advancement, and in the fifth year of Long'an he presumptuously styled himself King of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In his second year dragons and qilin appeared; in Long'an year 5 the ministers urged him to take the title King of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 其將鍮勿侖進曰：「昔我先君肇自幽、朔，被髮左衽，無冠冕之義，遷徙不常，無城邑之制，用能中分天下，威振殊境。

translations.literal: His general Tuyu Lun advanced and said: "In old days our former lord began from You and Shuo, with disheveled hair and garments buttoned on the left, without the meaning of caps and crowns, migrating without fixity, without the system of cities and walls—yet thereby he could divide the center of the realm and awe foreign borders."
translations.idiomatic: General Tuyu Lun said: "Our forebears rose from the north as nomads without cities, yet divided the realm."

sentences.zh: 今建大號，誠順天心。

translations.literal: "Now establishing the great title truly accords with Heaven's heart."
translations.idiomatic: "This great title accords with heaven."

sentences.zh: 然甯居樂士，非貽厥之規；

translations.literal: "Yet peaceful dwelling and happy soil is not the plan to bequeath to posterity;"
translations.idiomatic: "But peace alone is no legacy for sons;"

sentences.zh: 倉府粟帛，生敵人之志。

translations.literal: granaries of grain and silk breed the ambition of enemies.
translations.idiomatic: full granaries only whet enemies' appetite.

sentences.zh: 且首兵始號，事必無成，陳勝、項籍，前鑒不遠。

translations.literal: "Moreover he who first raises arms and first takes a title—affairs will surely not succeed; Chen Sheng and Xiang Yu—the recent mirror is not far."
translations.idiomatic: "First to rebel and first to crown oneself fails—remember Chen Sheng and Xiang Yu."

sentences.zh: 宜置晉人于諸城，勸課農桑，以供軍國之用，我則習戰法以誅未賓。

translations.literal: "We should place Jin people in the various cities, encourage farming and silkworms to supply army and state use; we then practice battle methods to punish those not yet submitted."
translations.idiomatic: "Settle Jin farmers in our towns for grain, and keep our warriors training to conquer the unsubdued."

sentences.zh: 若東西有變，長算以縻之；

translations.literal: If trouble arises east or west, use long-range plans to tie them down;
translations.idiomatic: If foes stir east or west, wear them down with patient strategy;

sentences.zh: 如其敵強於我，徙而以避其鋒，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: if the enemy is stronger than we, move aside to avoid their edge—is that not also good!
translations.idiomatic: if they outmatch us, withdraw and avoid their thrust—that is wise too!

sentences.zh: 」利鹿孤然其言。

translations.literal: Lilugu approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu agreed with Tuyu Lun.

sentences.zh: 於是率師伐呂隆，大敗之，獲其右僕射楊桓。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led troops to attack Lü Long, inflicted a great defeat, and captured his Right Vice Director Yang Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Lü Long, routed him, and took his Right Vice Director Yang Huan captive.

sentences.zh: 傉檀謂之曰：「安寢危邦，不思擇木，老為囚虜，豈曰智也！

translations.literal: Rutan said to him: "To sleep at ease in a perilous state, not to think of choosing a new roost, and in old age become a captive—is this called wisdom!"
translations.idiomatic: Rutan told him: "You slept easy in a doomed realm, never chose a worthier master, and ended a prisoner in old age—where is the wisdom in that?"

sentences.zh: 」桓曰：「受呂氏厚恩，位忝端貳，雖洪水滔天，猶欲濟彼俱溺，實恥為叛臣以見明主。

translations.literal: Huan said: "I received deep favor from the Lü house and rank unworthy of the second seat; though floods rise to the sky I still wish to save them and drown together—I would truly be ashamed to appear before a bright lord as a rebel minister."
translations.idiomatic: Huan replied: "The Lü house favored me and gave me high office; though the waters rose to heaven I meant to perish with them—I would be ashamed to stand before you as a turncoat."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀曰：「卿忠臣也！

translations.literal: Rutan said: "You are a loyal minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said: "You are a true loyalist!"

sentences.zh: 」以為左司馬。

translations.literal: He made him Left Major.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed him Left Major.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤謂其群下曰：「吾無經濟之才，忝承業統，自負乘在位，三載於茲。

translations.literal: Lilugu said to his ministers: "I lack talent for ordering the realm; I have presumptuously inherited the enterprise; counting from mounting the seat, three years have passed."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu told his ministers: "I have no gift for governing; I have unworthily taken the throne, and three years have passed since I did."

sentences.zh: 雖夙夜惟寅，思弘道化，而刑政未能允中，風俗尚多凋弊；

translations.literal: Though morning and night I am diligent, thinking to spread the Way and transform customs, punishments and government have not yet hit the mean, and customs still suffer much decay;"
translations.idiomatic: Though I toil day and night to spread order, justice is uneven and the people remain in decline;"

sentences.zh: 戎車屢駕，無辟境之功；

translations.literal: war-chariots have been driven repeatedly, yet there is no merit in opening the borders;"
translations.idiomatic: we have marched again and again, yet won no new territory;"

sentences.zh: 務進賢彥，而下猶蓄滯。

translations.literal: I sought to advance worthy men, yet below talent still stagnates."
translations.idiomatic: I have tried to promote talent, yet able men still languish below."

sentences.zh: 豈所任非才，將吾不明所致也？

translations.literal: Is it that those appointed lack talent, or that my lack of clarity has caused this?"
translations.idiomatic: Is it that I chose the wrong men, or that my own blindness is to blame?"

sentences.zh: 二三君子其極言無諱，吾將覽焉。

translations.literal: Gentlemen, speak to the utmost without reserve—I will examine it."
translations.idiomatic: Speak plainly, without holding back—I will hear you."

sentences.zh: 」祠部郎中史暠對曰：「古之王者，行師以全軍為上，破國次之，拯溺救焚，東征西怨。

translations.literal: Attendant of the Ancestral Shrine Shi Gao replied: "Ancient kings in campaigning ranked preserving the whole army first, destroying a state second; saving the drowning and rescuing from fire—east they march and west complains no more."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Gao of the Ancestral Shrine said: "Ancient kings prized sparing armies over smashing states; they rescued the drowning and those in fire—when they marched east, the west ceased to grumble."

sentences.zh: 今不以綏寧為先，惟以徙戶為務，安土重遷，故有離叛，所以斬將克城，土不加廣。

translations.literal: Now you do not put peace first but make relocating households your task; people love their soil and dread moving, hence desertion—thus though generals are slain and cities taken, the land does not grow wider."
translations.idiomatic: You put resettlement before peace; people cling to their homes and flee, so though you kill generals and take cities, your domain does not grow."

sentences.zh: 今取士拔才，必先弓馬，文章學藝為無用之條，非所以來遠人，垂不朽也。

translations.literal: In raising men you first require bow and horse; letters and arts count as useless—this is not how to draw men from afar or leave an unfading name."
translations.idiomatic: You choose men by bow and horse alone and treat learning as worthless—that will not win distant talent or a lasting name."

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：'不學禮，無以立。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Without learning ritual one cannot stand.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'Without ritual learning one cannot stand firm.'

sentences.zh: '宜建學校，開庠序，選耆德碩儒以訓胄子。

translations.literal: You should establish schools, open academies, and choose venerable great scholars to train the heir's sons."
translations.idiomatic: Found schools and academies, and set venerable scholars to teach the crown princes."

sentences.zh: 」利鹿孤善之，於是以田玄沖、趙誕為博士祭酒，以教胄子。

translations.literal: Lilugu approved; thereupon he appointed Tian Xuanchong and Zhao Yan as Libationer of the Masters of the Five Classics to teach the heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu accepted this and made Tian Xuanchong and Zhao Yan chief academicians to instruct the royal sons.

sentences.zh: 時利鹿孤雖僭位，尚臣姚興。

translations.literal: At that time though Lilugu had usurped the throne he still acknowledged vassalage to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lilugu had taken royal title, he still acknowledged Yao Xing as suzerain.

sentences.zh: 楊桓兄經佐命姚萇，早死，興聞桓有德望，征之。

translations.literal: Yang Huan's elder brother Jing had aided Yao Chang in founding his rule and died early; Xing heard Huan had virtue and prestige and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's brother Jing had helped Yao Chang found Later Qin and died young; hearing of Huan's reputation, Yao Xing summoned him.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤餞桓於城東，謂之曰：「本期與卿共成大業，事乖本圖，分歧之感，實情深古人。

translations.literal: Lilugu feasted Huan east of the city and said: "I had hoped to achieve the great work with you; affairs have gone against the original plan—the sense of parting is truly as deep as in the ancients' tales."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu gave Huan a farewell feast east of the city and said: "I meant to build an empire with you; fate has turned us aside—the pain of parting is as deep as any old story."

sentences.zh: 但鯤非溟海，無以運其軀；

translations.literal: But the leviathan is not the deep sea—it cannot move its body;"
translations.idiomatic: A great fish needs the ocean to swim;"

sentences.zh: 鳳非修梧，無以晞其翼。

translations.literal: the phoenix is not the tall parasol tree—it cannot dry its wings."
translations.idiomatic: a phoenix needs the high parasol tree to rest its wings."

sentences.zh: 卿有佐時之器，夜光之寶，當振纓雲閣，耀價連城，區區河右，未足以逞卿才力。

translations.literal: You have the instrument to aid the age, a jewel that gleams by night; you should shake your tassels in the cloud tower, shine with worth a city's ransom—mere west of the river is not enough to display your talent."
translations.idiomatic: You have the gifts to serve the age and jewels that outshine the night; you belong in the capital, worth a city in ransom—Hexi is too small for you."

sentences.zh: 善勖日新，以成大美。

translations.literal: Strive daily toward renewal to perfect the great beauty."
translations.idiomatic: Keep striving day by day, and you will fulfill your promise."

sentences.zh: 」桓泣曰：「臣往事呂氏，情節不建。

translations.literal: Huan wept: "I formerly served the Lü house and achieved no merit in my devotion."
translations.idiomatic: Huan wept: "I served the Lü house and failed them in my duty."

sentences.zh: 陛下宥臣于俘虜之中，顯同賢舊，每希攀龍附風，立尺寸之功，龍門既開，而臣違離，公衡之戀，豈曰忘之！

translations.literal: Your Majesty spared me among captives and honored me like an old worthy; I ever hoped to cling to dragon and phoenix and establish even a small merit—the dragon gate is opened yet I must part; the longing of Gongheng—how could I forget!"
translations.idiomatic: You spared me among prisoners and treated me as an old friend; I hoped to serve your dragon throne and earn some merit—now the gate opens and I must leave; my bond to you is no less than Gongheng's!"

sentences.zh: 」利鹿孤為之流涕。

translations.literal: Lilugu wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu wept with him.

sentences.zh: 遣傉檀又攻呂隆昌松太守孟禕于顯美，克之。

translations.literal: He sent Rutan again to attack Lü Long's Changsong prefect Meng Yi at Xianmei and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Rutan to attack Lü Long's Changsong prefect Meng Yi at Xianmei; Rutan took the city.

sentences.zh: 傉檀執禕而數之曰：「見機而作，賞之所先；

translations.literal: Rutan seized Yi and reproached him: "To act when the time appears is what reward puts first;"
translations.idiomatic: Rutan seized Yi and rebuked him: "Those who seize the moment are rewarded first;"

sentences.zh: 守迷不變，刑之所及。

translations.literal: to hold to error and not change is what punishment reaches."
translations.idiomatic: those who cling to folly when the tide turns face punishment."

sentences.zh: 吾方耀威玉門，掃平秦、隴，卿固守窮城，稽淹王憲，國有常刑，于分甘乎？

translations.literal: I am about to display might at Jade Gate and sweep Qin and Long—you stubbornly held this doomed city, delaying the royal statutes; the state has fixed punishments—are you content with your portion?"
translations.idiomatic: I mean to show my power at Jade Gate and pacify Qin and Long—you held a hopeless town and defied the king's law; the state has its penalties—do you accept your fate?"

sentences.zh: 」禕曰：「明公開翦河右，聲播宇內，文德以綏遠人，威武以懲不恪，況禕蔑爾，敢距天命！

translations.literal: Yi said: "The enlightened lord has opened Hexi, his fame fills the realm; civil virtue pacifies the distant, martial might punishes the disobedient—how could petty Yi dare resist Heaven's mandate!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said: "Your lordship has conquered Hexi and your fame fills the realm; civil virtue wins the distant, martial might chastises rebels—how could one as small as I resist Heaven's will!"

sentences.zh: 釁鼓之刑，禕之分也。

translations.literal: The crime of striking the war drums is Yi's portion.
translations.idiomatic: The penalty for taking up arms is mine to bear.

sentences.zh: 但忠於彼者，亦忠於此。

translations.literal: Yet he loyal to that one may also be loyal here.
translations.idiomatic: Yet loyalty to one master can become loyalty to another.

sentences.zh: 荷呂氏厚恩，受籓屏之任，明公至而歸命，恐獲罪于執事，惟公圖之。

translations.literal: Bearing deep debt to the Lü house, charged as a border shield; when the enlightened lord came I would have submitted, fearing guilt before your staff—only ask your plan."
translations.idiomatic: The Lü house favored me and made me a frontier guardian; when you came I wished to submit but feared your officers would condemn me—only you can judge."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀大悅，釋其縛，待之客禮。

translations.literal: Rutan was greatly pleased, loosed his bonds, and treated him with guest ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan was delighted, freed him, and received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 徙顯美、麗靬二千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: He moved more than two thousand households from Xianmei and Ligan and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled over two thousand households from Xianmei and Ligan and marched home.

sentences.zh: 嘉禕忠烈，拜左司馬。

translations.literal: Praising Yi's loyal sternness, he appointed him Left Major.
translations.idiomatic: Admiring Yi's steadfast loyalty, he made him Left Major.

sentences.zh: 禕請曰：「呂氏將亡，聖朝之並河右，昭然已定。

translations.literal: Yi requested: "The Lü house is about to perish; the holy court's swallowing of Hexi is clearly settled."
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked: "The Lü line is doomed; your dynasty's conquest of Hexi is already assured."

sentences.zh: 但為人守而不全，復忝顯任，竊所未安。

translations.literal: Yet having served as guardian and not completed it, then again receiving a lofty post—I secretly am uneasy."
translations.idiomatic: I failed as their guardian, yet you have given me high office—I cannot bear the shame."

sentences.zh: 明公之恩，聽禕就戮于姑臧，死且不朽。

translations.literal: By the enlightened lord's grace permit Yi to face execution at Guzang—death would yet be unfading."
translations.idiomatic: Grant me the grace to die at Guzang for the Lü house—then my death will have meaning."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀義而許之。

translations.literal: Rutan, moved by righteousness, agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his integrity, Rutan consented.

sentences.zh: 呂隆為沮渠蒙遜所伐，遣使乞師，利鹿孤引群下議之。

translations.literal: Lü Long was attacked by Juqu Mengxun and sent envoys begging troops; Lilugu gathered his ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun attacked Lü Long; Long sent envoys begging aid, and Lilugu called his ministers to council.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞婆衍侖曰：「今姑臧饑荒殘弊，谷石萬錢，野無青草，資食無取。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Po Yannalun said: "Now Guzang is famine-stricken and ruined; grain is ten thousand cash per picul, the wilds have no green grass, supplies cannot be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Po Yannalun, Left Assistant Director, said: "Guzang is starving and ruined—grain costs ten thousand cash a picul, the fields are bare, and there is nothing to supply an army."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜千里行師，糧運不屬，使二寇相殘，以乘其釁。

translations.literal: Mengxun marches a thousand li; grain transport will not connect—let the two foes maul each other and seize the opening."
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun has marched a thousand li; his supply lines will fail—let the two enemies tear each other apart, then strike."

sentences.zh: 若蒙遜拔姑臧，亦不能守，適可為吾取之，不宜救也。

translations.literal: If Mengxun takes Guzang he still cannot hold it—it would just be for us to take; we should not rescue."
translations.idiomatic: Even if Mengxun takes Guzang he cannot keep it—we should wait and take it ourselves, not rescue Long."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀曰：「侖知其一，未知其二。

translations.literal: Rutan said: "Lun knows one but not two."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said: "Lun sees only half the picture."

sentences.zh: 姑臧今雖虛弊，地居形勝，可西一都之會，不可使蒙遜據之，宜在速救。

translations.literal: Guzang though weakened lies in commanding terrain, the western capital's gathering point—we must not let Mengxun hold it; we should rescue at once."
translations.idiomatic: Guzang is weak but strategically vital—the key city of the west; we cannot let Mengxun have it—we must rescue now."

sentences.zh: 」利鹿孤曰：「車騎之言，吾之心也。

translations.literal: Lilugu said: "The Chariots-and-Cavalry's words are my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu said: "Rutan speaks my mind."

sentences.zh: 」遂遣傉檀率騎一萬救之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Rutan with ten thousand horse to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Rutan with ten thousand cavalry to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 至昌松而蒙遜已退，傉檀徙涼澤、段塚五百餘家而歸。

translations.literal: Reaching Changsong Mengxun had already withdrawn; Rutan moved more than five hundred households from Liangze and Duandui and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Changsong Mengxun had already retreated; Rutan resettled over five hundred families from Liangze and Duandui and returned.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤寢疾，令曰：「內外多虞，國機務廣，其令車騎嗣業，以成先王之志。

translations.literal: Lilugu fell gravely ill and ordered: "Within and without there are many cares, state affairs are weighty—let the Chariots-and-Cavalry succeed the enterprise to fulfill the former kings' aim."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu fell gravely ill and commanded: "Perils surround us and state business is heavy—let Rutan succeed me and fulfill our forefathers' ambition."

sentences.zh: 」在位三年而死，葬于西平之東南，偽諡曰康王。

translations.literal: After three years on the throne he died and was buried southeast of Xiping; his false posthumous title was King Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died after three years' reign and was buried southeast of Xiping, posthumously titled King Kang.

sentences.zh: 弟傉檀嗣。

translations.literal: His younger brother Rutan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Rutan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 禿髮傉檀

translations.literal: Tufa Rutan
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Tufa Rutan

sentences.zh: 傉檀少機警，有才略。

translations.literal: Rutan from youth was clever and alert, with talent and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Rutan was quick-witted and gifted with strategy.

sentences.zh: 其父奇之，謂諸子曰：「傉檀明識幹藝，非汝等輩也。

translations.literal: His father marveled at him and told his sons: "Rutan has bright insight and practical skill—not your sort."
translations.idiomatic: His father favored him and told his other sons: "Rutan has vision and ability—you are not his match."

sentences.zh: 」是以諸兄不以授子，欲傳之于傉檀。

translations.literal: Therefore the elder brothers would not pass the throne to their sons but wished to transmit it to Rutan.
translations.idiomatic: So his elder brothers refused to pass the throne to their own sons and meant to give it to Rutan.

sentences.zh: 及利鹿孤即位，垂拱而已，軍國大事皆以委之。

translations.literal: When Lilugu took the throne he merely held his hands folded; all great affairs of army and state were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lilugu reigned he merely held court in name; Rutan handled all military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 以元興元年僭號涼王，遷于樂都，改元曰弘昌。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing he presumptuously styled himself King of Liang, moved to Ledu, and changed the era to Hongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxing year 1 he took the title King of Liang, moved the capital to Ledu, and proclaimed the era Hongchang.

sentences.zh: 初，乞伏乾歸之在晉興也，以世子熾磐為質。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qifu Gangui was at Jinxing he left his heir Chibpan as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Qifu Gangui was at Jinxing, he left his heir Chibpan as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 後熾磐逃歸，為追騎所執，利鹿孤命殺之。

translations.literal: Later Chibpan fled home, was seized by pursuing horse, and Lilugu ordered his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chibpan escaped; pursuers caught him, and Lilugu ordered him killed.

sentences.zh: 傉檀曰：「臣子逃歸君父，振古通義，故魏武善關羽之奔，秦昭恕頃襄之逝。

translations.literal: Rutan said: "A minister fleeing back to his lord and father is an ancient universal norm; hence Cao of Wei favored Guan Yu's flight, and King Zhao of Qin forgave King Qingxiang's departure."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said: "A son fleeing home to his father is an ancient right—Cao Cao honored Guan Yu's return, and King Zhao of Qin pardoned King Qingxiang's flight."

sentences.zh: 熾磐雖逃叛，孝心可嘉，宜垂全宥，以弘海嶽之量。

translations.literal: Though Chibpan fled in rebellion his filial heart is praiseworthy; you should extend full pardon to display the breadth of sea and mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Chibpan fled from loyalty to his father; spare him and show the magnanimity of a true king."

sentences.zh: 」乃赦之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: They pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 至是，熾磐又奔允街，傉檀歸其妻子。

translations.literal: At this time Chibpan again fled to Yunjie; Rutan returned his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: When Chibpan fled again to Yunjie, Rutan sent back his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 姚興遣使拜傉檀車騎將軍、廣武公。

translations.literal: Yao Xing sent envoys to appoint Rutan General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent envoys appointing Rutan General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 傉檀大城樂都。

translations.literal: Rutan greatly fortified Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan built up Ledu into a great fortress.

sentences.zh: 姚興遣將齊難率眾迎呂隆于姑臧，傉檀攝昌松、魏安二戍以避之。

translations.literal: Yao Xing sent the general Qi Nan with troops to welcome Lü Long at Guzang; Rutan evacuated the garrisons of Changsong and Wei'an to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent Qi Nan to install Lü Long at Guzang; Rutan withdrew from the garrisons at Changsong and Wei'an to avoid a clash.

sentences.zh: 興涼州刺史王尚遣主薄宗敞來聘。

translations.literal: Xing's Governor of Liang Wang Shang sent Registrar Zong Chang on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang, Yao Xing's governor of Liang, sent his registrar Zong Chang on a diplomatic visit.

sentences.zh: 敞父燮，呂光時自湟河太守入為尚書郎，見傉檀于廣武，執其手曰：「君神爽宏拔，逸氣陵雲，命世之傑也，必當克清世難。

translations.literal: Chang's father Xie, in Lü Guang's time from Governor of Huanghe entered as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; meeting Rutan at Guangwu he grasped his hand: "My lord's spirit is grand and towering, transcendent breath pierces the clouds—a hero of the age who will surely sweep away the world's troubles."
translations.idiomatic: Chang's father Xie had served Lü Guang as governor of Huanghe and later as Master of Writing; meeting Rutan at Guangwu he took his hand and said: "Your spirit towers above others, your force pierces the clouds—you are a hero of the age who will pacify the realm."

sentences.zh: 恨吾年老不及見耳，以敞兄弟托君。

translations.literal: I regret my old age will not see it—I entrust Chang and his brothers to you."
translations.idiomatic: I am too old to see it myself—I leave my sons Chang and his brothers in your care."

sentences.zh: 」至是，傉檀謂敞曰：「孤以常才，謬為尊先君所見稱，每自恐有累大人水鏡之明。

translations.literal: Now Rutan said to Chang: "I with ordinary talent was mistakenly praised by your honored late father; I ever feared I would stain the great man's mirror-bright judgment."
translations.idiomatic: Now Rutan told Chang: "Your late father praised me beyond my worth; I feared I would disappoint his keen judgment."

sentences.zh: 及忝家業，竊有懷君子。

translations.literal: Taking the family enterprise I have secretly held you in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took power I have kept you in my thoughts.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：'中心藏之，何日忘之。

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'In the heart I store it—what day do I forget?'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, 'I treasure it in my heart—when shall I forget?'

sentences.zh: '不圖今日得見卿也。

translations.literal: I never thought today I would meet you."
translations.idiomatic: I never dreamed I would see you today."

sentences.zh: 」敞曰：「大王仁侔魏祖，存念先人，雖硃暉眄張堪之孤，叔向撫汝齊之子，無以加也。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Great King's benevolence matches the Wei founder's; remembering our forebear—even Zhu Hui's glance at Zhang Kan's orphan, Shuxiang's care for Ruqi's son—add nothing more."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "Your kindness rivals the Wei founder's remembrance of old friends—greater than Zhu Hui's care for Zhang Kan's orphan or Shuxiang's for Ruqi's son."

sentences.zh: 」酒酣，語及平生。

translations.literal: When wine was deep they spoke of their whole lives.
translations.idiomatic: As the wine flowed they talked of their lives.

sentences.zh: 傉檀曰：「卿魯子敬之儔，恨不與卿共成大業耳。」

translations.literal: Rutan said: "You are Lu Zijing's peer—I regret not achieving the great work with you."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said: "You are the equal of Lu Su—I regret we could not build an empire together."

sentences.zh: 傉檀以姚興之盛，又密圖姑臧，乃去其年號，罷尚書丞郎官，遣參軍關尚聘於興。

translations.literal: Rutan, because Yao Xing was strong and he secretly plotted Guzang, dropped his era name, abolished Masters of Writing assistants and clerks, and sent Aide Guan Shang as envoy to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yao Xing was powerful and Rutan secretly planned to take Guzang, he dropped his era title, dissolved the secretariat, and sent Guan Shang as envoy to Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 興謂尚曰：「車騎投誠獻款，為國籓屏，擅興兵眾，輒造大城，為臣之道固若是乎？

translations.literal: Xing said to Shang: "The Chariots-and-Cavalry offers sincerity and tribute, shield of the realm—yet he arms troops at will and suddenly builds a great city; is this how a minister should act?"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing told Shang: "Rutan pledges loyalty and guards my frontier—yet he raises troops at will and builds a great fortress; is this how a vassal behaves?"

sentences.zh: 」尚曰：「王侯設險以自固，先王之制也，所以安人衛眾，預備不虞。

translations.literal: Shang said: "Lords set barriers to strengthen themselves—former kings' institutions—to settle the people, guard the host, and prepare for the unforeseen."
translations.idiomatic: Shang replied: "Princes fortify their borders by ancient custom—to protect their people and guard against surprise."

sentences.zh: 車騎僻在遐籓，密邇勍寇，南則逆羌未賓，西則蒙遜跋扈，蓋為國家重門之防，不圖陛下忽以為嫌。

translations.literal: The Chariots-and-Cavalry lies in a remote border, close to fierce foes; south the rebellious Qiang are unsubdued, west Mengxun is overbearing—this is the state's outer gate; I never thought Your Majesty would suddenly take offense."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan sits on a distant frontier beside powerful enemies—the Qiang rebel in the south, Mengxun threatens in the west; his walls are the realm's outer gate—I did not expect Your Majesty to take offense."

sentences.zh: 」興笑曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: Xing smiled: "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing smiled and said: "You speak well."

sentences.zh: 傉檀遣其將文支討南羌、西虜，大破之。

translations.literal: Rutan sent his general Wen Zhi to campaign against the southern Qiang and western foreigners and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan sent Wen Zhi against the southern Qiang and western tribes and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 上表姚興，求涼州，不許，加傉檀散騎常侍，增邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He memorialized Yao Xing requesting Liang Province; it was not granted; Rutan was given Regular Attendant Within the Fast and his fief increased by two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned Yao Xing for Liang Province but was refused; Xing made him Regular Attendant and added two thousand households to his fief.

sentences.zh: 傉檀於是率師伐沮渠蒙遜，次於氐池。

translations.literal: Rutan thereupon led troops against Juqu Mengxun and halted at Dichi.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan then marched against Juqu Mengxun and camped at Dichi.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜嬰城固守，芟其禾苗，至於赤泉而還。

translations.literal: Mengxun shut the city and held firm; Rutan cut his grain shoots and returned as far as Chiquan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun held his walls; Rutan ravaged his crops and withdrew to Chiquan.

sentences.zh: 獻興馬三千匹，羊三萬頭。

translations.literal: He presented Xing three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yao Xing three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep as tribute.

sentences.zh: 興乃署傉檀為使持節、都督河右諸軍事、車騎大將軍、領護匈奴中郎將、涼州刺史，常侍、公如故，鎮姑臧。

translations.literal: Xing then appointed Rutan Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all armies of the Hexi, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Leader of the Captain Who Protects the Xiongnu, Governor of Liang—Regular Attendant and ducal rank as before—and garrisoned Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing then appointed Rutan commander of Hexi armies, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Protector of the Xiongnu, and Governor of Liang, with his former titles intact, and posted him at Guzang.

sentences.zh: 傉檀率步騎三萬次於五澗，興涼州刺史王尚遣辛晁、孟禕、彭敏出迎。

translations.literal: Rutan led thirty thousand infantry and horse and halted at Wujian; Xing's Governor Wang Shang sent Xin Chao, Meng Yi, and Peng Min to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan advanced with thirty thousand men to Wujian; Wang Shang sent Xin Chao, Meng Yi, and Peng Min to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 尚出自清陽門，鎮南文支入自涼風門。

translations.literal: Wang Shang went out from Qingyang Gate; the Defender of the South Wen Zhi entered from Liangfeng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang departed through Qingyang Gate while Wen Zhi, Defender of the South, entered through Liangfeng Gate.

sentences.zh: 宗敞以別駕送尚還長安，傉檀曰：「吾得涼州三千餘家，情之所寄，唯卿一人，奈何舍我去乎？

translations.literal: Zong Chang as Acting Administrator escorted Shang back to Chang'an; Rutan said: "Gaining Liang Province's three thousand-plus households, the one my heart rests on is you alone—how can you leave me?"
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chang, as acting administrator, escorted Wang Shang to Chang'an; Rutan said: "I have won three thousand households of Liang, but you alone are dear to me—how can you leave?"

sentences.zh: 」敞曰：「今送舊君，所以忠於殿下。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Now escorting the former lord is how I am loyal to Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: Chang replied: "Escorting my old master is how I remain loyal to you."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀曰：「吾今新牧貴州，懷遠安邇之略，為之若何？

translations.literal: Rutan said: "I am newly governing this noble province—policy to embrace the distant and settle the near—what would you do?"
translations.idiomatic: Rutan asked: "I am new to governing this province—how would you win the distant and settle those near?"

sentences.zh: 」敞曰：「涼土雖弊，形勝之地，道由人弘，實在殿下。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Liang's soil though worn is a land of strategic advantage; the Way is carried by men—it truly rests with Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "Liang is worn but strategically strong; its fate depends on its ruler—and that is you."

sentences.zh: 段懿、孟禕、武威之宿望；

translations.literal: Duan Yi and Meng Yi are famed elders of Wuwei;"
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yi and Meng Yi are respected elders of Wuwei;"

sentences.zh: 辛晁、彭敏，秦、隴之冠冕；

translations.literal: Xin Chao and Peng Min are the crown and cap of Qin and Long;
translations.idiomatic: Xin Chao and Peng Min are the finest men of Qin and Long;

sentences.zh: 斐敏、馬輔，中州之令族；

translations.literal: Fei Min and Ma Fu are eminent clans of the Central Plains;
translations.idiomatic: Fei Min and Ma Fu come from leading families of the heartland;

sentences.zh: 張昶，涼國之舊胤；

translations.literal: Zhang Chang is an old scion of the Liang state;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang is a descendant of the former Liang royal house;

sentences.zh: 張穆、邊憲、文齊、楊班、梁崧、趙昌，武同飛、羽。

translations.literal: Zhang Mu, Bian Xian, Wen Qi, Yang Ban, Liang Song, and Zhao Chang—in martial prowess equal Fei and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mu, Bian Xian, Wen Qi, Yang Ban, Liang Song, and Zhao Chang are warriors to rival Zhang Fei and Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 以大王之神略，撫之以威信，農戰並修，文教兼設，可以從橫於天下，河右豈足定乎！

translations.literal: With Your Highness's divine strategy, governing them with awe-inspiring trust, cultivating farming and war together and establishing culture and arms alike, you may roam the realm at will—is merely settling the River Right enough!
translations.idiomatic: With your genius and authority, if you unite agriculture and war and pair civil rule with military strength, you can dominate the world—why settle for the Hexi alone!

sentences.zh: 」傉檀大悅，賜敞馬二十匹。

translations.literal: " Rutan was greatly pleased and gifted Chang twenty horses.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan was delighted and gave Chang twenty horses.

sentences.zh: 於是大饗文武于謙光殿，班賜金馬各有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon he held a great feast for civil and military officials in Qian'guang Hall and distributed gold and horses to each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He then feasted his officials in Qian'guang Hall and rewarded them with gold and horses in graded shares.

sentences.zh: 遣西曹從事史暠聘于姚興。

translations.literal: He sent Western Cao Attendant Shi Hao as envoy to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Shi Hao of the Western Bureau as envoy to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 興謂暠曰：「車騎坐定涼州，衣錦本國，其德我乎？

translations.literal: Xing said to Hao: "The Chariots-and-Cavalry has secured Liangzhou and returned in brocade to his homeland—does he owe me gratitude?
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing asked Hao: "Rutan has taken Liangzhou and come home in glory—does he owe me thanks?

sentences.zh: 」暠曰：「車騎積德河西，少播英問，王威未接，投誠萬里，陛下官方任才，量功授職，彝倫之常，何德之有！

translations.literal: " Hao said: "The Chariots-and-Cavalry accumulated virtue in Hexi and spread his fame little; Your Majesty's majesty had not yet reached him, and he pledged loyalty from ten thousand li away. Your Majesty appoints men by office and bestows posts by merit—it is the constant law of human order; what gratitude is owed!
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied: "Rutan built his reputation in Hexi long before your authority reached him; he submitted from afar. You assign office by talent and rank by merit—that is only proper. What debt does he owe?

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「朕不以州授車騎者，車騎何從得之。

translations.literal: " Xing said: "If I had not granted the province to the Chariots-and-Cavalry, how would he have obtained it?
translations.idiomatic: Xing said: "Had I not given him the province, how would he have gained it?

sentences.zh: 」暠曰：「使河西雲擾、呂氏顛狽者，實由車騎兄弟傾其根本。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "That Hexi was clouded with turmoil and the Lü house overthrown was truly because the Chariots-and-Cavalry and his brothers overturned their foundations.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "Hexi fell into chaos and the Lü house collapsed because Rutan and his brothers destroyed them from within.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖鴻羅遐被，涼州猶在天網之外。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty's vast net covers distant lands, Liangzhou was still outside heaven's net.
translations.idiomatic: Though your power spans the realm, Liangzhou long lay beyond your reach.

sentences.zh: 故征西以周、召之重，力屈姑臧；

translations.literal: Thus the Campaigning-in-the-West, with the weight of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, had his strength broken at Guzang;
translations.idiomatic: Your western expedition, though led by men of Zhou and Shao's stature, was broken at Guzang;

sentences.zh: 齊難以王旅之盛，勢挫張掖。

translations.literal: Qilian Cheng, with the emperor's armies in full strength, had his momentum checked at Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: and Qilian Cheng, at the head of your imperial host, was turned back at Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 王尚孤城獨守，外逼群狄，陛下不連兵十年，殫竭中國，涼州未易取也。

translations.literal: Wang Shang held a lone city, pressed without by many Di; had Your Majesty not sent armies for ten years and exhausted the Central Realm, Liangzhou would not have been easily taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang held out alone, beset by barbarians; without ten years of war and the draining of the heartland, you could not have taken Liangzhou easily.

sentences.zh: 今以虛名假人，內收大利，乃知妙算自天，聖與道合，雖云遷授，蓋亦時宜。

translations.literal: Now granting an empty title to another while inwardly reaping great profit—this shows divine calculation from heaven and sagehood united with the Way; though called a transfer of appointment, it was surely timely.
translations.idiomatic: Now you grant him a hollow title yet keep the real gain—heaven's design and the sage's way. Though you call it a transfer, the timing was perfect.

sentences.zh: 」興悅其言，拜騎都尉。

translations.literal: " Xing was pleased with his words and appointed him Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing was pleased and made Hao Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 傉檀宴群僚於宣德堂，仰視而歎曰：「古人言作者不居，居者不作，信矣。

translations.literal: Rutan feasted his ministers in Xuan'ede Hall, looked up, and sighed: "The ancients said, 'He who makes it does not dwell in it; he who dwells in it does not make it'—how true.
translations.idiomatic: At a feast in Xuan'ede Hall, Rutan looked up and sighed: "The ancients were right: builders do not keep what they build, and those who inherit seldom built it.

sentences.zh: 」孟禕進曰：「張文王築城苑，繕宗廟，為貽厥之資，萬世之業，秦師濟河，漼然瓦解。

translations.literal: " Meng Yi advanced: "Duke Wen of Zhang built cities and parks and repaired ancestral temples as legacy for his heirs and an enterprise for ten thousand generations—when Qin armies crossed the river, it collapsed in torrents.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yi said: "Duke Wen of Zhang built walls, parks, and temples for his heirs' sake—yet when Qin crossed the Yellow River, his realm dissolved overnight.

sentences.zh: 梁熙據全州之地，擁十萬之眾，軍敗於酒泉，身死于彭濟。

translations.literal: Liang Xi held all the province and commanded a hundred thousand; his army was defeated at Jiuquan and he died at Pengji.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi ruled the whole province with a hundred thousand men—yet he was beaten at Jiuquan and died at Pengji.

sentences.zh: 呂氏以排山之勢，王有西夏，率土崩離，銜璧秦、雍。

translations.literal: The Lü house, with momentum to topple mountains, ruled western Xia; when all the land collapsed, they came bearing jade to Qin and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The Lü clan, who seemed strong enough to move mountains and ruled western Xia, fell apart and surrendered to Qin and Yong with jade disks at their necks.

sentences.zh: 寬饒有言：'富貴無常，忽輒易人。

translations.literal: Kuang Rao said: 'Wealth and nobility have no constancy; in a moment they change hands.
translations.idiomatic: As Kuang Rao said, 'Fortune and rank never stay fixed; they pass to another in an instant.

sentences.zh: '此堂之建，年垂百載，十有二主，唯信順可以久安，仁義可以永固，願大王勉之。

translations.literal: ' This hall has stood nearly a hundred years with twelve lords; only trust and compliance bring long peace, and only benevolence and righteousness bring lasting strength—may Your Highness strive in these."
translations.idiomatic: ' This hall is nearly a century old and has had twelve masters. Only faithfulness and obedience secure long rule; only benevolence and righteousness endure. I urge you to heed this."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀曰：「非君無以聞讜言也。

translations.literal: " Rutan said: "Without you I would not have heard such loyal counsel."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said: "Without you I would never have heard such honest advice."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀雖受制于姚興，然車服禮章一如王者。

translations.literal: Though Rutan was constrained by Yao Xing, his chariots, raiment, and ritual were all like a king's.
translations.idiomatic: Though subject to Yao Xing, Rutan kept royal chariots, dress, and ceremony.

sentences.zh: 以宗敞為太府主簿、錄記室事。

translations.literal: He made Zong Chang Master of the Palace Treasury clerk and recorder of secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zong Chang clerk of the palace treasury and head of the secretariat staff.

sentences.zh: 傉檀偽遊澆河，襲徙西平、湟河諸羌三萬餘戶于武興、番禾、武威、昌松四郡。

translations.literal: Rutan feigned touring the Jiao River, then suddenly relocated more than thirty thousand households of the Qiang of Xiping and Huang River to the four commanderies of Wuxing, Fanhe, Wuwei, and Changsong.
translations.idiomatic: Pretending to tour the Jiao River, Rutan forcibly moved over thirty thousand Qiang households from Xiping and Huanghe into Wuxing, Fanhe, Wuwei, and Changsong.

sentences.zh: 徵集戎夏之兵五萬餘人，大閱于方亭，遂伐沮渠蒙遜，入西陝。

translations.literal: He gathered more than fifty thousand troops of barbarian and Han, held a grand review at Fangting, then attacked Juqu Mengxun and entered Western Shan.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered fifty thousand mixed troops, reviewed them at Fangting, then marched against Juqu Mengxun into Western Shan.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜率眾來距，戰于均石，為蒙遜所敗。

translations.literal: Mengxun led troops to resist; they fought at Junshi and Rutan was defeated by Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun met him at Junshi and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 傉檀率騎二萬，運谷四萬石以給西郡。

translations.literal: Rutan led twenty thousand horse and transported forty thousand shi of grain to supply Western Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan led twenty thousand cavalry and hauled forty thousand shi of grain to provision Western Commandery.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜攻西郡，陷之。

translations.literal: Mengxun attacked Western Commandery and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun then stormed Western Commandery and captured it.

sentences.zh: 其後傉檀又與赫連勃勃戰于陽武，為勃勃所敗，將佐死者十餘人，傉檀與數騎奔南山，幾為追騎所得。

translations.literal: Afterward Rutan again fought Helian Bobo at Yangwu and was defeated; more than ten generals and attendants died; Rutan fled to the southern mountains with a few horsemen and was nearly caught by pursuers.
translations.idiomatic: Later Rutan fought Helian Bobo at Yangwu and lost again; a dozen officers died, and he barely escaped to the southern hills with a handful of riders.

sentences.zh: 傉檀懼東西寇至，徙三百里內百姓入于姑臧，國中駭怨。

translations.literal: Rutan feared foes east and west would come, moved all people within three hundred li into Guzang, and the realm was alarmed and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing attack from both sides, he forced everyone within three hundred li into Guzang; the whole state panicked and seethed.

sentences.zh: 屠各成七兒因百姓之擾也，率其屬三百人，叛傉檀於北城。

translations.literal: Tugu Cheng Qier, because of the people's distress, led his three hundred followers and rebelled against Rutan at North City.
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting the unrest, Tugu Cheng Qier led three hundred men in revolt at the north city.

sentences.zh: 推梁貴為盟主，貴閉門不應。

translations.literal: They made Liang Gui league leader; Gui shut his door and would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: They tried to make Liang Gui their leader, but he barred his gates and refused.

sentences.zh: 一夜眾至數千。

translations.literal: In one night the crowd reached several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By nightfall their numbers had swelled to several thousand.

sentences.zh: 殿中都尉張猛大言於眾曰：「主上陽武之敗，蓋恃眾故也。

translations.literal: Palace Commandant Zhang Meng spoke loudly to the crowd: "Our lord's defeat at Yangwu was because he trusted in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Meng, commandant of the palace guard, shouted to the rebels: "Our lord lost at Yangwu because he relied on sheer numbers.

sentences.zh: 責躬悔過，明君之義，諸君何故從此小人作不義之事！

translations.literal: To examine oneself and repent is a bright lord's duty—why follow these petty men in unrighteous deed!
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler examines his faults—that is your duty. Why follow these nobodies into treason!

sentences.zh: 殿內武旅正爾相尋，目前之危，悔將無及。

translations.literal: The palace guards are just now hunting you down—the danger before your eyes; regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: The palace troops are already on your trail. Disaster is at hand, and remorse will come too late."

sentences.zh: 」眾聞之，咸散。

translations.literal: " When the crowd heard this, all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: At his words the mob scattered.

sentences.zh: 七兒奔晏然，殿中騎將白路等追斬之。

translations.literal: Qier fled toward Yanran; Palace Cavalry General Bai Lu and others pursued and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qier fled toward Yanran; Bai Lu and other palace cavalry chased him down and killed him.

sentences.zh: 軍諮祭酒梁裒、輔國司馬邊憲等七人謀反，傉檀悉誅之。

translations.literal: Army Advisor Libationer Liang Pou, Assisting-State Major Bian Xian, and seven others plotted rebellion; Rutan executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Pou, Bian Xian, and five others plotted revolt; Rutan had all seven put to death.

sentences.zh: 姚興以傉檀外有陽武之敗，內有邊、梁之亂，遣其尚書郎韋宗來觀釁。

translations.literal: Yao Xing, because Rutan had outward the Yangwu defeat and inward the Bian and Liang troubles, sent his Secretariat Gentleman Wei Zong to observe for openings.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Rutan weakened by defeat at Yangwu and unrest within, Yao Xing sent Secretariat Gentleman Wei Zong to probe for weakness.

sentences.zh: 傉檀與宗論六國從橫之規，三家戰爭之略，遠言天命廢興，近陳人事成敗，機變無窮，辭致清辯。

translations.literal: Rutan with Zong discussed the Six States' vertical and horizontal alliances and the Three Kingdoms' war stratagems, spoke afar of heaven's mandate in rise and fall and spoke near of human affairs' success and failure—infinite stratagems, clear and eloquent diction.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan debated with Wei Zong the alliances of the Warring States and the strategies of the Three Kingdoms, spoke of dynastic fate and practical politics, and showed endless wit in lucid, polished speech.

sentences.zh: 宗出而歎曰：「命世大才、經綸名教者，不必華宗夏士；

translations.literal: Zong went out and sighed: "He who commands an age's great talent and orders the famous teachings need not be a splendid clan's summer scholar;
translations.idiomatic: Leaving, Wei Zong sighed: "A man who shapes an age and guides civilization need not be a pedigreed Han scholar;

sentences.zh: 撥煩理亂、澄氣濟世者，亦未必《八索》、《九丘》。

translations.literal: one who disperses troubles, orders chaos, clears the air and aids the world need not necessarily be versed in the Eight Cords and Nine Hillocks.
translations.idiomatic: nor must one who settles turmoil and steadies the realm be learned in the Eight Cords and Nine Hillocks.

sentences.zh: 五經之外，冠冕之表，復自有人。

translations.literal: Beyond the Five Classics, in the outer court of the crowned, there are still such men.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Five Classics and the court's inner circle, such men still exist.

sentences.zh: 車騎神機秀髮，信一代之偉人，由余、日磾豈足為多也！

translations.literal: The Chariots-and-Cavalry—motion divine, hair splendid—is truly a generation's great man; You Yu and Jinti Shi are hardly worth mentioning beside him!
translations.idiomatic: Rutan's mind is keen and his bearing noble—a true giant of the age. You Yu and Jinti Shi pale beside him!

sentences.zh: 」宗還長安，言於興曰：「涼州雖殘弊之後，風化未頹，傉檀權詐多方，憑山河之固，未可圖也。

translations.literal: " Zong returned to Chang'an and told Xing: "Though Liangzhou is worn after ruin, its customs are not yet decayed; Rutan is crafty in many ways and relies on rivers and mountains' strength—not to be plotted against."
translations.idiomatic: Back in Chang'an, Wei Zong told Yao Xing: "Liangzhou is battered but not broken; Rutan is cunning and holds the mountains and rivers. Do not move against him."

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「勃勃以烏合之眾尚能破之，吾以天下之兵，何足克也！

translations.literal: " Xing said: "Bobo with a rabble host could still defeat him—with the realm's armies, how is he not conquerable!"
translations.idiomatic: Xing said: "If Bobo with a mob could beat him, how can my imperial armies fail!

sentences.zh: 」宗曰：「形移勢變，終始殊途，陵人者易敗，自守者難攻。

translations.literal: " Zong said: "Form shifts, momentum changes, beginning and end take different paths—he who bullies others is easily beaten; he who holds himself firm is hard to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zong replied: "Circumstances change. The aggressor is easily beaten; the defender who digs in is hard to dislodge.

sentences.zh: 陽武之役，傉檀以輕勃勃致敗。

translations.literal: At Yangwu, Rutan by underrating Bobo brought defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan lost at Yangwu because he underestimated Bobo.

sentences.zh: 今以大軍臨之，必自固求全，臣竊料群臣無傉檀匹也。

translations.literal: Now with a great army upon him he will surely fortify and seek survival—I privately reckon none among his ministers matches Rutan.
translations.idiomatic: Faced with your main force he will hold fast and fight to survive. None of his ministers equals him.

sentences.zh: 雖以天威臨之，未見其利。

translations.literal: Though imperial majesty presses upon him, I see no gain."
translations.idiomatic: Even with heaven's might behind you, I see little profit."

sentences.zh: 」興不從，乃遣其將姚弼及斂成等率步騎三萬來伐，又使其將姚顯為弼等後繼，遺傉檀書云「遣尚書左僕射齊難討勃勃，懼其西逸，故令弼等於河西邀之。

translations.literal: " Xing did not listen; he sent his generals Yao Bi and Qilian Cheng and others leading thirty thousand foot and horse to attack, and also sent his general Yao Xian as rear support for Bi, writing Rutan: "I sent Left Vice Director Qi Nan to campaign against Bobo, fearing he would flee west, hence I ordered Bi and others to intercept him in Hexi."
translations.idiomatic: Xing ignored him. He sent Yao Bi and Qilian Cheng with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry, with Yao Xian in support, and wrote Rutan: "I have sent Qi Nan against Bobo and fear he may flee west, so Bi is posted in Hexi to block him."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀以為然，遂不設備。

translations.literal: " Rutan believed it and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan believed him and let his guard down.

sentences.zh: 弼眾至漠口，昌松太守蘇霸嬰城固守，弼喻霸令降，霸曰：「汝違負盟誓，伐委順之籓，天地有靈，將不祐汝！

translations.literal: Bi's host reached Mokou; Changsong Administrator Su Ba held the city firm; Bi persuaded Ba to surrender; Ba said: "You betray your oath and attack a submitting vassal—heaven and earth have spirit; they will not aid you!
translations.idiomatic: At Mokou, Changsong's governor Su Ba shut the gates. When Bi demanded surrender, Su Ba said: "You break your oath and strike a loyal vassal—heaven will not bless you!

sentences.zh: 吾甯為涼鬼，何降之有！

translations.literal: I would rather be a Liang ghost—why would I surrender!
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die a ghost of Liang than yield!

sentences.zh: 」城陷，斬霸。

translations.literal: " The city fell; Ba was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell and Su Ba was executed.

sentences.zh: 弼至姑臧，屯於西苑。

translations.literal: Bi reached Guzang and encamped at Western Park.
translations.idiomatic: Bi advanced to Guzang and camped in the Western Park.

sentences.zh: 州人王鐘、宋鐘、王娥等密為內應，候人執其使送之。

translations.literal: Provincials Wang Zhong, Song Zhong, Wang E, and others secretly acted as inside allies; scouts seized their messenger and delivered him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhong, Song Zhong, Wang E, and others plotted treason with the enemy; scouts caught their messenger and turned him in.

sentences.zh: 傉檀欲誅其元首，前軍伊力延侯曰：「今強敵在外，內有奸豎，兵交勢踧，禍難不輕，宜悉坑之以安內外。

translations.literal: Rutan wished to execute the ringleaders; Forward Army Yili Yanhou said: "Now strong foes are without, traitors within, armies engaged and momentum urgent—disaster is not light; all should be buried alive to secure within and without."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan meant to kill the plotters. Yili Yanhou of the vanguard said: "With the enemy outside and traitors inside, the crisis is grave. Execute them all to steady the realm."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀從之，殺五千餘人，以婦女為軍賞。

translations.literal: " Rutan agreed; more than five thousand were killed and women given as army rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan agreed. Over five thousand were slaughtered, and their women were handed out as booty to the troops.

sentences.zh: 命諸郡縣悉驅牛羊於野，斂成縱兵虜掠。

translations.literal: He ordered all commanderies to drive cattle and sheep into the fields; Qilian Cheng let troops loot.
translations.idiomatic: He had every district drive livestock into the open, and Qilian Cheng's men plundered freely.

sentences.zh: 傉檀遣其鎮北俱延、鎮軍敬歸等十將率騎分擊，大敗之，斬首七千餘級。

translations.literal: Rutan sent his Pacifier of the North Ju Yan, Pacifying Army Jing Gui, and ten generals with horse in separate attacks; great defeat—heads cut more than seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan sent Ju Yan, Jing Gui, and ten other generals with cavalry in separate strikes and routed them, taking more than seven thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 姚弼固壘不出，傉檀攻之未克，乃斷水上流，欲以持久斃之。

translations.literal: Yao Bi held the ramparts and would not come out; Rutan attacked but could not take it; he cut off the river's upper flow, wishing to kill them by prolonged siege.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Bi held his fort and refused battle. Unable to storm it, Rutan dammed the river upstream to starve them out.

sentences.zh: 會雨甚，堰壞，弼軍乃振。

translations.literal: Heavy rain came; the dam broke; Bi's army revived.
translations.idiomatic: A great storm burst the dam, and Bi's army recovered.

sentences.zh: 姚顯聞弼敗，兼道赴之，軍勢甚盛。

translations.literal: Yao Xian heard Bi was defeated and marched by doubled routes—his army's momentum very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Bi's defeat, Yao Xian hurried to the front with a powerful host.

sentences.zh: 遣射將孟欽等五人挑戰於涼風門，弦未及發，材官將軍宋益等馳擊斬之。

translations.literal: He sent archer generals Meng Qin and five others to challenge at Liangfeng Gate; before strings were drawn, Weapons-Officer General Song Yi and others galloped and struck them down.
translations.idiomatic: He sent five archers, including Meng Qin, to challenge at Liangfeng Gate; before they could draw, Song Yi and other officers charged out and cut them down.

sentences.zh: 顯乃委罪斂成。

translations.literal: Xian then laid blame on Qilian Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xian blamed the defeat on Qilian Cheng.

sentences.zh: 遣使謝傉檀，引師而歸。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to apologize to Rutan and withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to apologize to Rutan and pulled his army back.

sentences.zh: 傉檀於是僭即涼王位，赦其境內，改年為嘉平，置百官。

translations.literal: Rutan thereupon usurped the title King of Liang, amnestied his realm, changed the era to Jiaping, and established the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan then declared himself King of Liang, proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the era name Jiaping, and installed a full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 立夫人折掘氏為五後，世子武台為太子、錄尚書事，左長史趙晁、右長史郭倖為尚書左右僕射，鎮北俱延為太尉，鎮軍敬歸為司隸校尉，自余封署各有差。

translations.literal: He made Lady Zhejue one of five queens, heir Wutai crown prince and recorder of Masters of Writing, Left Chief Clerk Zhao Chao and Right Chief Clerk Guo Xing Left and Right Vice Directors, Pacifier of the North Ju Yan Grand Marshal, Pacifying Army Jing Gui Metropolitan Commandant—the rest enfeoffed and appointed each to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He made Lady Zhejue one of five consorts, named his heir Wutai crown prince and head of the secretariat, appointed Zhao Chao and Guo Xing as left and right vice directors, Ju Yan as grand marshal, Jing Gui as metropolitan commandant, and ranked the rest accordingly.

sentences.zh: 遣其左將軍枯木、駙馬都尉胡康伐沮渠蒙遜，掠臨松人千餘戶而還。

translations.literal: He sent his Left General Kumu and Commandant of the Horse Escort Hu Kang to attack Juqu Mengxun, plundered more than a thousand households at Linshong, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Kumu and Hu Kang against Juqu Mengxun; they raided Linshong, carried off over a thousand families, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜大怒，率騎五千至於顯美方亭，破車蓋鮮卑而還。

translations.literal: Mengxun in great rage led five thousand horse to Xianmei's Fangting, broke the Chegai Xianbei, and returned.
