translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Mengxun led five thousand cavalry to Fangting in Xianmei, crushed the Chegai Xianbei, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俱延又伐蒙遜，大敗而歸。

translations.literal: Ju Yan again attacked Mengxun and returned in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Yan attacked Mengxun again and was routed.

sentences.zh: 傉檀將親率眾伐蒙遜，趙晁及太史令景保諫曰：「今太白未出，歲星在西，宜以自守，難以伐人。

translations.literal: Rutan was about to lead troops personally against Mengxun; Zhao Chao and Grand Clerk Jing Bao remonstrated: "Now the White Star has not risen, the Year Star is in the west—one should hold to self-defense; hard to attack others."
translations.idiomatic: When Rutan prepared to march against Mengxun in person, Zhao Chao and the grand astrologer Jing Bao warned: "Venus has not yet risen and Jupiter stands in the west. Defend yourself; do not attack."

sentences.zh: 比年天文錯亂，風霧不時，唯修德責躬可以甯吉。

translations.literal: In recent years celestial signs are confused, winds and mists untimely—only cultivate virtue and examine the self can bring peace.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's signs have been erratic for years, winds and fogs ill-timed. Only by cultivating virtue and examining your own conduct can you secure good fortune.

sentences.zh: 」傉檀曰：「蒙遜往年無狀，入我封畿，掠我邊疆，殘我禾稼。

translations.literal: " Rutan said: "Mengxun in past years acted shamelessly, entered my borders, plundered my frontiers, and ruined my grain.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said: "Mengxun has repeatedly violated my borders, raided my frontiers, and destroyed my crops.

sentences.zh: 吾蓄力待時，將報東門之恥，今大軍已集，卿欲沮眾邪？

translations.literal: I stored strength awaiting the moment to avenge the shame of the eastern gate—now the great army is gathered—do you wish to dampen the host?
translations.idiomatic: I have waited for the chance to avenge the humiliation at the eastern gate. The army is ready—are you trying to discourage them?

sentences.zh: 」保曰：「陛下不以臣不肖，使臣主察乾象，若見事不言，非為臣之體。

translations.literal: " Bao said: "Your Majesty did not deem me unworthy but made me oversee the heavenly signs—if I see matters and do not speak, that is not a minister's way."
translations.idiomatic: Bao said: "You appointed me to read the heavens. If I see danger and stay silent, I fail my office."

sentences.zh: 天文顯然，動必無利。

translations.literal: The celestial signs are clear—movement will surely bring no profit."
translations.idiomatic: The stars are plain: any campaign will end badly."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀曰：「吾以輕騎五萬伐之，蒙遜若以騎兵距我，則眾寡不敵；

translations.literal: " Rutan said: "I with fifty thousand light horse attack—if Mengxun meets me with cavalry, numbers cannot match;
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said: "With fifty thousand light cavalry I will strike. If he meets me with horse alone, I outnumber him;

sentences.zh: 兼步而來，則舒疾不同；

translations.literal: if he mixes foot soldiers coming, then slow and fast differ;
translations.idiomatic: if he brings infantry as well, his pace will be uneven;

sentences.zh: 救右則擊其左，赴前則攻其後，終不與之交兵接戰，卿何懼乎？

translations.literal: rescue the right then strike his left, rush forward then attack his rear—in the end I will not join battle with him face to face—what do you fear?
translations.idiomatic: I will hit his left when he saves his right, strike his rear when he advances—I need never fight a pitched battle. What is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 」保曰：「天文不虛，必將有變。

translations.literal: " Bao said: "Heavenly signs do not lie—change will surely come."
translations.idiomatic: Bao said: "The heavens do not lie. Disaster is certain."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀怒，鎖保而行，曰：「有功當殺汝以徇，無功封汝百戶侯，」既而蒙遜率眾來距，戰於窮泉，傉檀大敗，單馬奔還。

translations.literal: " Rutan in anger shackled Bao and marched, saying: "If there is merit I shall kill you as example; if no merit I ennoble you Marquis of a Hundred Households"—soon Mengxun led troops to resist; they fought at Qiongquan; Rutan was greatly defeated and fled back alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Rutan chained Bao and marched, saying: "Win and I execute you as a warning; lose and I make you marquis of a hundred households." Mengxun met him at Qiongquan and crushed him; Rutan fled home alone.

sentences.zh: 景保為蒙遜所擒，讓之曰：「卿明于天文，為彼國所任，違天犯順，智安在乎？

translations.literal: Jing Bao was seized by Mengxun, who rebuked him: "You are bright at astronomy, employed by that state—you defy heaven and violate compliance; where is wisdom?
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun captured Jing Bao and reproached him: "You read the stars for that court yet served a ruler who defied heaven. Where was your wisdom?

sentences.zh: 」保曰：「臣匪為無智，但言而不從。

translations.literal: " Bao said: "It is not that I lacked wisdom but that I spoke and was not heeded."
translations.idiomatic: Bao replied: "I was not without counsel—my lord simply would not listen."

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜曰：「昔漢祖困于平城，以婁敬為功；

translations.literal: " Mengxun said: "Formerly Han Founder was trapped at Pingcheng and made Lou Jing's counsel merit;
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun said: "When the Han founder was trapped at Pingcheng, he rewarded Lou Jing;

sentences.zh: 袁紹敗於官渡，而田豐為戮。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao was defeated at Guandu and Tian Feng was executed."
translations.idiomatic: when Yuan Shao lost at Guandu, he killed Tian Feng."

sentences.zh: 卿策同二子，貴主未可量也。

translations.literal: Your strategy matches both men—the value of your lord cannot be measured."
translations.idiomatic: Your advice fits both tales—your master's worth is hard to judge."

sentences.zh: 卿必有婁敬之賞者，吾今放卿，但恐有田豐之禍耳。

translations.literal: You will surely have Lou Jing's reward—I release you now, but I fear your lord may deal you Tian Feng's fate."
translations.idiomatic: You deserve Lou Jing's reward, and I set you free—but your lord may yet treat you like Tian Feng."

sentences.zh: 」保曰：「寡君雖才非漢祖，猶不同本初，正可不得封侯，豈慮禍也。

translations.literal: " Bao said: "Our lord though not talented as Han Founder is still unlike Yuan Benchu—I may simply fail to win a marquisate, but why worry of calamity?
translations.idiomatic: Bao said: "My lord is no Liu Bang, but he is no Yuan Shao either. I may miss a marquisate, but I do not fear execution.

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜乃免之。

translations.literal: " Mengxun then released him.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun let him go.

sentences.zh: 至姑臧，傉檀謝之曰：「卿，孤之蓍龜也，而不能從之，孤之深罪。

translations.literal: Reaching Guzang, Rutan apologized: "You are my divining tortoise and milfoil, yet I could not follow you—my deep fault."
translations.idiomatic: Back in Guzang, Rutan said to him: "You were my oracle, and I would not heed you—that was my grave error.

sentences.zh: 」封保安亭侯。

translations.literal: " He enfeoffed him Marquis of Bao'an Precinct.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed him as Marquis of Bao'an Precinct.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜進圖姑臧，百姓懲東苑之戮，悉皆驚散。

translations.literal: Mengxun advanced to attack Guzang; the people, remembering the slaughter at Eastern Park, all fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun pressed on Guzang. Remembering the massacre in the Eastern Park, the people fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 壘掘、麥田、車蓋諸部盡降于蒙遜。

translations.literal: The tribes of Leijue, Maitian, Chegai, and others all submitted to Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: The Leijue, Maitian, Chegai, and other tribal groups all surrendered to Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 傉檀遣使請和，蒙遜許之，乃遣司隸校尉敬歸及子他為質，歸至胡坑，逃還，他為追兵所執。

translations.literal: Rutan sent envoys to request peace; Mengxun agreed and sent Censor-in-Chief Jing Gui and his son Ta as hostages; at Hukeng Jing Gui fled back, and Ta was seized by pursuing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan sued for peace; Mengxun accepted and sent Jing Gui, Censor-in-Chief, with his son Ta as hostages. At Hukeng Jing Gui escaped; pursuers captured Ta.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜徙其眾八千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: Mengxun moved more than eight thousand households and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun resettled eight thousand-odd households and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 右衛折掘奇鎮據石驢山以叛。

translations.literal: Right Guard Zhejue Qi Jizhen seized Shilu Mountain and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jizhen of the Right Guard Zhejue rebelled and held Shilu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 傉檀懼為蒙遜所滅，又慮奇鎮克嶺南，乃遷于樂都，留大司農成公緒守姑臧。

translations.literal: Rutan feared destruction by Mengxun and also feared Qi would take the lands south of the ridge; he moved to Ledu and left Grand Minister of Agriculture Cheng Gongxu to guard Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Mengxun would destroy him and Qi would seize the southern passes, Rutan moved to Ledu and left Cheng Gongxu, Grand Minister of Agriculture, to hold Guzang.

sentences.zh: 傉檀始出城，焦諶、王侯等閉門作難，收合三千餘家，保據南城。

translations.literal: As Rutan was about to leave the city, Jiao Chen, Wang Hou, and others shut the gates and raised trouble, gathering more than three thousand families to hold the south city.
translations.idiomatic: As Rutan left the city, Jiao Chen and Wang Hou shut the gates in revolt, rallying three thousand families behind the south wall.

sentences.zh: 諶推焦朗為大都督、龍驤大將軍，諶為涼州刺史，降于蒙遜。

translations.literal: Chen installed Jiao Lang as Grand Commander and Dragon Cavalry Grand General; Chen as Governor of Liang, and submitted to Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Chen made Jiao Lang Grand Commander and Dragon Cavalry Grand General, took the governorship of Liang himself, and surrendered to Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍敬歸討奇鎮于石驢山，戰敗，死之。

translations.literal: Pacifying Army Jing Gui attacked Qi Jizhen at Shilu Mountain, was defeated, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Gui of the Pacifying Army attacked Qi at Shilu Mountain, was routed, and killed.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜因克姑臧之威來伐，傉檀遣其安北段苟、左將軍雲連乘虛出番禾以襲其後，徙三千餘家于西平。

translations.literal: Mengxun came to attack exploiting his capture of Guzang; Rutan sent his Pacifier of the North Duan Gou and Left General Yun Lian to strike Fanhe in his rear and moved more than three thousand families to Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun marched on the strength of Guzang; Rutan sent Duan Gou and Yun Lian to raid Fanhe from behind and resettled three thousand families in Xiping.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜圍樂都，三旬不克，遣使謂傉檀曰：「若以寵子為質，我當還師。

translations.literal: Mengxun besieged Ledu; after thirty days without taking it he sent envoys telling Rutan: "If you give a favored son as hostage I shall withdraw the army."
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun besieged Ledu for thirty days in vain, then sent word: "Give me a beloved son as hostage and I will withdraw."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀曰：「去否任卿兵勢。

translations.literal: Rutan said: "Whether I stay or go is yours to decide by force of arms."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan replied: "Stay or go—as your armies please."

sentences.zh: 卿違盟無信，何質以供！

translations.literal: You break oath and lack faith—what hostage have I to offer!"
translations.idiomatic: You broke faith—what hostage could I offer you!"

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜怒，築室返耕，為持久之計。

translations.literal: Mengxun in anger built houses and turned to farming, planning a long siege.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun in fury built houses and turned the soil, settling in for a long siege.

sentences.zh: 群臣固請，乃以子安周為質。

translations.literal: His ministers urgently pressed him; only then did he give his son Anzhou as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers pressed him hard; at last he gave his son Anzhou as hostage.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜引歸。

translations.literal: Mengxun withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun broke the siege and marched away.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾樹洛幹率眾來伐，傉檀遣其太子武台距之，為洛幹所敗。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun Shuluogan led troops to attack; Rutan sent his heir Wutai to resist and was defeated by Shuluogan.
translations.idiomatic: Shuluogan of the Tuyuhun attacked; Rutan sent his heir Wutai to meet him and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 傉檀又將伐蒙遜，邯川護軍孟愷諫曰：「蒙遜初並姑臧，凶勢甚盛，宜固守伺隙，不可妄動。

translations.literal: Rutan was again about to campaign against Mengxun; Han River Protector Meng Kai remonstrated: "Mengxun has newly swallowed Guzang and his ferocious momentum is very strong—you should hold firm and watch for an opening, not act rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan prepared to strike Mengxun again; Meng Kai, Han River Protector, warned: "Mengxun has just taken Guzang and his power is at its peak—hold fast and wait; do not move rashly."

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 五道俱進，至番禾、苕藋，掠五千餘戶。

translations.literal: Five columns advanced together to Fanhe and Tiaodiao, seizing more than five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Five columns marched to Fanhe and Tiaodiao and seized more than five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 其將屈右進曰：「陛下轉戰千里，前元完陣，徙戶資財，盈溢衢路，宜倍道旋師，早度峻險。

translations.literal: His general Qu You advanced and said: "Your Majesty has campaigned a thousand li; the van is intact, households and goods overflow the roads—you should march at double speed and cross the steep passes early."
translations.idiomatic: General Qu You urged: "You have marched a thousand li with the van unbroken and booty choking the roads—double the pace and cross the passes while you can."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜善於用兵，士眾習戰，若輕軍卒至，出吾慮表，大敵外逼，徙戶內攻，危之道也。

translations.literal: Mengxun is skilled in war and his troops are seasoned in battle; if light forces suddenly arrive beyond our reckoning, a great enemy pressing outside and resettled households attacking within—that is the path of peril."
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun is a master of war and his men are hardened; if light troops strike where we do not expect, the foe without and the settlers within will crush us—that is the road to ruin."

sentences.zh: 」衛尉伊力延曰：「我軍勢方盛，將士勇氣自倍，彼徒我騎，勢不相及，若倍道旋師，必捐棄資財，示人以弱，非計也。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Guard Yiliyan said: "Our army's momentum is at its height and officers and men are doubly brave; they are foot and we are horse—the conditions do not compare. If we double back we must abandon goods and show weakness to men—that is no plan."
translations.idiomatic: Yiliyan, Commandant of the Guard, said: "Our army is at flood tide and every man fights twice as hard; infantry cannot match our horse. To turn back is to abandon plunder and show fear—that is no plan."

sentences.zh: 」屈右出而告其諸弟曰：「吾言不用，天命也。

translations.literal: Qu You went out and told his brothers: "My words are not used—this is Heaven's decree."
translations.idiomatic: Qu You left and told his brothers: "They will not hear me—this is fate."

sentences.zh: 此吾兄弟死地。

translations.literal: This is where we brothers will die."
translations.idiomatic: Here we brothers will die."

sentences.zh: 」俄而昏霧風雨，蒙遜軍大至，傉檀敗績而還。

translations.literal: Soon dusk fog and wind and rain came; Mengxun's army arrived in force; Rutan was defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon fog, wind, and rain closed in; Mengxun's host fell upon them; Rutan was routed and fled home.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜進圍樂都，傉檀嬰城固守，以子染幹為質，蒙遜乃歸，久之，遣安西紇勃耀兵西境。

translations.literal: Mengxun advanced to besiege Ledu; Rutan held the walls; he gave his son Ran Gan as hostage; Mengxun withdrew. Long afterward he sent Pacifier of the West Hebo to display troops on the western border.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun besieged Ledu again; Rutan held the walls and gave his son Ran Gan as hostage; Mengxun withdrew. Later he sent Hebo, Pacifier of the West, to parade troops on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜侵西平，徙戶掠牛馬而還。

translations.literal: Mengxun invaded Xiping, moved households, plundered cattle and horses, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun raided Xiping, carried off families and livestock, and returned.

sentences.zh: 邯川護軍孟愷表鎮南、湟河太守文支荒酒愎諫，不血阝政事。

translations.literal: Han River Protector Meng Kai memorialized that Defender of the South and Governor of Huang River Wen Zhi was reckless with wine, obstinate in counsel, and neglected government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Kai memorialized that Wen Zhi, Defender of the South and Governor of Huang River, drank without measure, spurned good counsel, and neglected his duties.

sentences.zh: 傉檀謂伊力延曰：「今州土傾覆，所杖者文支而已，將若之何？

translations.literal: Rutan said to Yiliyan: "Now the province is overturned; all I rely on is Wen Zhi alone—what shall I do?"
translations.idiomatic: Rutan asked Yiliyan: "The province is ruined; Wen Zhi is all I have left—what can I do?"

sentences.zh: 」延曰：「宜召而訓之，使改往修來。

translations.literal: Yiliyan said: "You should summon and instruct him to reform his past and improve his conduct."
translations.idiomatic: Yiliyan said: "Summon him, rebuke him, and make him mend his ways."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀乃召文支，既到，讓之曰：「二兄英姿早世，吾以不才嗣統，不能負荷大業，顛狽如是，胡顏視世，雖存若隕。

translations.literal: Rutan summoned Wen Zhi; when he arrived he reproached him: "Two elder brothers died young in splendor; I, unworthy, succeeded and cannot bear the great enterprise, so fallen as this—how can I face the world! Though alive I am as if fallen."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan summoned Wen Zhi and rebuked him: "My brilliant elder brothers died young; I, unfit, inherited and have brought the realm to ruin—how can I show my face! I live as one already dead."

sentences.zh: 庶憑子鮮存衛，藉文種復吳，卿之謂也。

translations.literal: I hoped to rely on Zixian to guard the realm and on Wen Zhong to restore Wu—you were that man."
translations.idiomatic: I counted on you as Zixian to guard the state and as Wen Zhong to restore Wu."

sentences.zh: 聞卿唯酒是耽，荒廢庶事。

translations.literal: I hear you drown yourself only in wine and abandon all duties.
translations.idiomatic: They say you drink your days away and abandon every duty.

sentences.zh: 吾年已老，卿復若斯，祖宗之業將誰寄也。

translations.literal: I am already old and you are again like this—upon whom shall the ancestors' enterprise be entrusted!"
translations.idiomatic: I am old, and you are still like this—who will carry our fathers' work!"

sentences.zh: 」文支頓首陳謝。

translations.literal: Wen Zhi bowed and confessed fault.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhi kowtowed and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 邯川人衛章等謀殺孟愷，南啟乞伏熾磐。

translations.literal: Han River men Wei Zhang and others plotted to kill Meng Kai and southward opened relations with Qifu Chibpan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhang of Han River plotted to kill Meng Kai and sent word south to Qifu Chibpan.

sentences.zh: 郭越止之曰：「孟尹寬以惠下，何罪而殺之！

translations.literal: Guo Yue stopped them saying: "Chief Minister Meng is generous to those below—what crime warrants killing him!"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yue stopped them: "Minister Meng is generous to his men—what crime could justify his murder!"

sentences.zh: 吾寧違眾而死，不負君以生。

translations.literal: I would rather die against the multitude than live by betraying my lord."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die with the crowd against me than live by betraying my lord."

sentences.zh: 」乃密告之愷，誘章等飲酒，殺四十餘人。

translations.literal: He secretly informed Kai, lured Zhang and the rest to drink, and killed more than forty.
translations.idiomatic: He warned Meng Kai in secret, lured Zhang and his fellows to drink, and killed more than forty.

sentences.zh: 愷懼熾磐軍之至，馳告文支，文支遣將軍匹珍赴之。

translations.literal: Kai feared Chibpan's army would arrive and galloped to inform Wen Zhi; Wen Zhi sent General Pi Zhen to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Chibpan's approach, Meng Kai rode to Wen Zhi; Wen Zhi sent General Pi Zhen to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 熾磐軍到城，聞珍將至，引歸。

translations.literal: When Chibpan's army reached the city and heard Pi Zhen was coming they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chibpan reached the city, heard Pi Zhen was marching, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜又攻樂都，二旬不克而還。

translations.literal: Mengxun again attacked Ledu; after twenty days without taking it he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun besieged Ledu again, failed in twenty days, and left.

sentences.zh: 鎮南文支以湟河降蒙遜，徙五千餘戶于姑臧。

translations.literal: Defender of the South Wen Zhi surrendered Huang River to Mengxun, who moved more than five thousand households to Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhi surrendered Huang River to Mengxun, who resettled five thousand households at Guzang.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜又來伐，傉檀以太尉俱延為質，蒙遜乃引還。

translations.literal: Mengxun again came to attack; Rutan gave Grand Marshal Juyan as hostage; Mengxun then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun attacked again; Rutan gave Grand Marshal Juyan as hostage, and Mengxun withdrew.

sentences.zh: 傉檀議欲西征乙弗，孟愷諫曰：「連年不收，上下饑弊，南逼熾磐，北迫蒙遜，百姓騷動，下不安業。

translations.literal: Rutan deliberated a western campaign against the Yifu; Meng Kai remonstrated: "Years without harvest, above and below hungry and exhausted, pressed in the south by Chibpan and in the north by Mengxun—the people are unsettled and below there is no secure livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan planned a western campaign against the Yifu; Meng Kai warned: "Famine has drained us; Chibpan presses from the south, Mengxun from the north—the people are in turmoil and cannot live in peace."

sentences.zh: 今遠征雖克，後患必深，不如結盟熾磐，通糴濟難，慰喻雜部，以廣軍資，畜力繕兵，相時而動。

translations.literal: Now though a distant campaign may succeed, later troubles will surely be deep; better to ally with Chibpan, exchange grain to relieve hardship, comfort and instruct the various tribes to broaden army supplies, store strength and repair weapons, and move when the time is right."
translations.idiomatic: Even victory abroad will breed disaster at home; ally with Chibpan, buy grain, win over the tribes, hoard strength and sharpen arms, and strike only when the moment is ripe."

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：'其亡其亡，系于苞桑。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'About to perish, about to perish—bound to the mulberry in the bud.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: 'Ruin is near, ruin is near—tie yourself to the mulberry while it is still in bud.'

sentences.zh: '惟陛下圖之。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty consider this."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, weigh this well."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀曰：「孤將略地，卿無沮眾。

translations.literal: Rutan said: "I mean to seize territory—do not discourage the troops."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said: "I am going to take land—do not dampen the army's spirit."

sentences.zh: 」謂其太子武台曰：「今不種多年，內外俱窘，事宜西行，以拯此弊。

translations.literal: He told his heir Wutai: "Years without planting—within and without we are destitute—the time calls for a western march to save this distress."
translations.idiomatic: He told his heir Wutai: "Years without sowing have beggared us inside and out—a western march is our only rescue."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜近去，不能卒來，旦夕所慮，唯在熾盤。

translations.literal: Mengxun has lately withdrawn and cannot come at once; what I fear morning and evening is only Chibpan."
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun has just withdrawn and cannot strike at once; only Chibpan troubles me day and night."

sentences.zh: 彼名微眾寡，易以討禦，吾不過一月，自足周旋。

translations.literal: Their name is slight and their masses few—easy to resist; within a month I shall have room enough to maneuver."
translations.idiomatic: His fame is small and his host few—he is easy to beat; within a month I shall be free to turn back."

sentences.zh: 汝謹守樂都，無使失墮。

translations.literal: Guard Ledu carefully and do not let it fall."
translations.idiomatic: Hold Ledu fast and do not let it fall."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀乃率騎七千襲乙弗，大破之，獲牛馬羊四十餘萬。

translations.literal: Rutan led seven thousand cavalry to strike the Yifu, inflicted a great defeat, and obtained more than four hundred thousand cattle, sheep, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan led seven thousand horse against the Yifu, routed them, and took four hundred thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 熾磐乘虛來襲，撫軍從事中郎尉肅言于武台曰：「今外城廣大，難以固守，宜聚國人於內城，肅等率諸晉人距戰於外，如或不捷，猶有萬全。

translations.literal: Chibpan seized the opening and struck; Adjunct to the Pacifying Army Wei Su said to Wutai: "The outer city is vast and hard to defend—you should gather our people within the inner city; Su and others will lead the Jin men to fight outside; if we do not prevail there is still full safety."
translations.idiomatic: Chibpan struck while Rutan was away; Wei Su, adjunct to the Pacifying Army, urged Wutai: "The outer city is too wide to hold—gather our people within the inner wall; we Jin will fight outside, and even if we lose, the core remains safe."

sentences.zh: 」武台曰：「小賊蕞爾，旦夕當走，卿何慮之過也。

translations.literal: Wutai said: "A petty bandit, a mere nib—he will flee in a morning and evening; your worry is excessive."
translations.idiomatic: Wutai said: "A petty thief—he will run by tomorrow; you worry too much."

sentences.zh: 」武台懼晉人有二心也，乃召豪望有勇謀者閉之於內。

translations.literal: Wutai feared the Jin men had divided hearts and called influential men of courage and counsel to shut them within.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Jin would turn traitor, Wutai locked the brave and wise within the inner city.

sentences.zh: 孟愷泣曰：「熾磐不道，人神同憤，愷等進則荷恩重遷，退顧妻子之累，豈有二乎！

translations.literal: Meng Kai wept: "Chibpan is unrighteous; men and spirits share rage; if we advance we bear the grace of heavy relocation, if we retreat we glance at the burden of wife and children—how could there be two hearts!"
translations.idiomatic: Meng Kai wept: "Chibpan is a villain; heaven and earth rage with us. Advance, and we repay your grace for moving us here; retreat, and we think of our wives and children—how could we be divided!"

sentences.zh: 今事已急矣，人思自效，有何猜邪？

translations.literal: The affair is urgent now; men wish to give their all—what suspicion is there!"
translations.idiomatic: The crisis is upon us; every man longs to die fighting—why doubt us!"

sentences.zh: 」武台曰：「吾豈不知子忠，實懼餘人脫生慮表，以君等安之耳。

translations.literal: Wutai said: "I do not fail to know your loyalty; I truly fear others may live by escaping beyond reckoning—to settle you I act thus."
translations.idiomatic: Wutai said: "I know you are loyal; I fear others may slip away in panic—that is why I confine you, to keep you safe."

sentences.zh: 」一旬而城潰。

translations.literal: In ten days the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the city fell.

sentences.zh: 安西樊尼自西平奔告傉檀，傉檀謂眾曰：「今樂都為熾磐所陷，男夫盡殺，婦女賞軍，雖欲歸還，無所赴也。

translations.literal: Pacifier of the West Fanni fled from Xiping to tell Rutan; Rutan said to the crowd: "Now Ledu is lost to Chibpan; men are all killed, women rewarded to the army—though we wish to return, there is nowhere to go."
translations.idiomatic: Fanni fled from Xiping with the news; Rutan told his men: "Chibpan has taken Ledu; the men are dead, the women given to his soldiers—even if we turn back, we have nowhere left."

sentences.zh: 卿等能與吾藉乙弗之資，取契汗以贖妻子者，是所望也。

translations.literal: If you can with me use Yifu resources to take Qihan and ransom wife and children, that is my hope."
translations.idiomatic: If you will follow me west, use the Yifu to seize Qihan, and buy back your wives and children—that is my hope."

sentences.zh: 不爾，歸熾磐便為奴僕矣，豈忍見妻子在他人懷抱中！

translations.literal: Otherwise, returning to Chibpan means becoming slaves and servants—how can I bear to see wife and children in another's embrace!"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise we submit to Chibpan as slaves—how can I bear to see our wives in another's arms!"

sentences.zh: 」遂引師而西，眾多逃返，遣鎮北段苟追之，苟亦不還。

translations.literal: He led the army west; many fled back; he sent Pacifier of the North Duan Gou to pursue; Gou also did not return.
translations.idiomatic: He marched west; many deserted on the road; he sent Duan Gou to bring them back, but Gou never returned.

sentences.zh: 於是將士皆散，惟中軍紇勃、後軍洛肱、安西樊尼、散騎侍郎陰利鹿在焉。

translations.literal: Then officers and men all scattered; only Central Army Hebo, Rear Army Luogong, Pacifier of the West Fanni, and Gentleman Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Yin Lili remained.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men melted away; only Hebo, Luogong, Fanni, and Yin Lili, Gentleman Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, stayed.

sentences.zh: 傉檀曰：「蒙遜、熾磐昔皆委質於吾，今而歸之，不亦鄙哉！

translations.literal: Rutan said: "Mengxun and Chibpan in old days both pledged allegiance to me—now to go to them, is it not base!"
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said: "Mengxun and Chibpan once pledged themselves to me—now to crawl to them, how shameful!"

sentences.zh: 四海之廣，匹夫無所容其身，何其痛也！

translations.literal: The broad four seas—there is nowhere for a lone man to shelter his body; how painful!"
translations.idiomatic: All beneath heaven, and not one corner for a single man—how bitter!"

sentences.zh: 蒙遜與吾名齊年比，熾磐姻好少年，俱其所忌，勢皆不濟。

translations.literal: Mengxun and I are peers in name and years; Chibpan is a young man bound by marriage alliance—both are what they fear; neither situation can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun is my peer in rank and age; Chibpan is a young kinsman by marriage—each fears me; neither road can save me."

sentences.zh: 與其聚而同死，不如分而或全。

translations.literal: Rather than gather and die together, better to divide and perhaps some survive."
translations.idiomatic: Better to split and live in part than die together in a heap."

sentences.zh: 樊尼長兄之子，宗部所寄，吾眾在北者戶垂二萬，蒙遜方招懷遐邇，存亡繼絕，汝其西也。

translations.literal: Fanni is my elder brother's son, the tribe's reliance; our households in the north number near twenty thousand; Mengxun is now recruiting the distant and continuing the severed line—you go west."
translations.idiomatic: Fanni is my brother's son and the tribe's hope; twenty thousand of our people remain in the north; Mengxun is winning the distant and restoring the broken line—go west."

sentences.zh: 紇勃、洛肱亦與尼俱。

translations.literal: Hebo and Luogong go with Ni."
translations.idiomatic: Hebo and Luogong, go with Fanni."

sentences.zh: 吾年老矣，所適不容，甯見妻子而死！

translations.literal: I am old; where I am suited does not admit me; I would rather see wife and children and die!"
translations.idiomatic: I am old; no land will have me; I would rather see my wife and children and die!"

sentences.zh: 」遂歸熾磐，唯陰利鹿隨之。

translations.literal: He then submitted to Chibpan; only Yin Lili followed him.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Chibpan; only Yin Lili followed.

sentences.zh: 傉檀謂利鹿曰：「去危就安，人之常也。

translations.literal: Rutan said to Lili: "Leaving danger for safety is man's constant."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan told Lili: "To flee danger for safety is only human."

sentences.zh: 吾親屬皆散，卿何獨留？

translations.literal: My kin are all scattered—why do you alone remain!"
translations.idiomatic: My kin have all fled—why do you alone stay!"

sentences.zh: 」利鹿曰：「臣老母在家，方寸實亂。

translations.literal: Lili said: "Your servant's old mother is at home; my heart is truly in turmoil."
translations.idiomatic: Lili said: "My old mother is at home; my heart is torn."

sentences.zh: 但忠孝之義，勢不俱全。

translations.literal: But loyalty and filial duty cannot both be fully achieved in this situation."
translations.idiomatic: Yet loyalty and filial piety cannot both be whole in such a day."

sentences.zh: 雖不能西哭沮渠，申包胥之誠；

translations.literal: Though I cannot weep west of the Qu for Juqu as Shen Baoxu did;
translations.idiomatic: I cannot weep west of the Qu for Juqu as Shen Baoxu did for Chu;

sentences.zh: 東感秦援，展毛遂之操，負羈靮而侍陛下者，臣之分也。

translations.literal: nor feel Qin's aid in the east and display Mao Sui's resolve, yet to bear bridle and serve Your Majesty at your side—that is your servant's portion."
translations.idiomatic: nor win Qin from the east and show Mao Sui's courage, yet to take bridle and serve at your side—that is my duty."

sentences.zh: 惟願開弘遠猷，審進止之算。

translations.literal: I only hope you will open a far-reaching design and weigh advance and retreat."
translations.idiomatic: Only grant me this: think far, and weigh every move."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀歎曰：「知人固未易，人亦未易知。

translations.literal: Rutan sighed: "To know men is truly not easy, and men are not easily known."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan sighed: "To know a man is hard; to be known is harder still."

sentences.zh: 大臣親戚皆棄我去，終紿不虧者，唯卿一人。

translations.literal: Ministers and kin all left me; in the end none failed me but you alone."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and kin abandoned me; in the end only you did not fail me."

sentences.zh: 歲寒不凋，見之於卿。

translations.literal: The cold of year does not wither the pine—shown in you."
translations.idiomatic: The pine does not fade in winter—that is you."

sentences.zh: 」傉檀至西平，熾磐遣使郊迎，待以上賓之禮。

translations.literal: Rutan reached Xiping; Chibpan sent envoys to welcome him in the suburbs and treated him as a guest of highest honor.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiping, Chibpan's envoys met him beyond the walls and received him as a guest of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 初，樂都之潰也，諸城皆降於熾磐，傉檀將尉賢政固守浩亹不下。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ledu fell, all cities submitted to Chibpan; Rutan's general Wei Xianzheng held Hao'e and would not descend.
translations.idiomatic: When Ledu fell, every city surrendered to Chibpan; only Wei Xianzheng held Hao'e and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 熾磐呼之曰：「樂都已潰，卿妻子皆在吾間，孤城獨守，何所為也！

translations.literal: Chibpan called to him: "Ledu has already fallen; your wife and children are all in my grasp—a lone city held alone, what are you doing!"
translations.idiomatic: Chibpan called: "Ledu is lost; your wife and children are mine—why hold a lone city!"

sentences.zh: 」賢政曰：「受涼王厚恩，為國家籓屏，雖知樂都已陷，妻子為擒，先歸獲賞，後順受誅，然不知主上存亡，未敢歸命。

translations.literal: Xianzheng said: "I received deep favor from the King of Liang and served the state as a border shield; though I know Ledu has fallen and wife and children are captives, to submit first wins reward and to follow later wins punishment—yet not knowing whether my lord lives or dies I dare not return to allegiance."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzheng said: "The King of Liang favored me; I was his border shield. I know Ledu has fallen and my family is captive—the first to submit is rewarded, the last is punished—but I do not know whether my lord lives or dies, and I dare not yield yet."

sentences.zh: 妻子小事，豈足動懷！

translations.literal: Wife and children are a small matter—how could they move my heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Wife and children are a small thing—they cannot sway me!"

sentences.zh: 昔羅憲待命，晉文亮之；

translations.literal: In old times Luo Xian awaited orders and Jin Wen praised him;
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xian waited for his orders and Jin Wen honored him;

sentences.zh: 文聘後來，魏武不責。

translations.literal: Wen Pi came later and Cao of Wei did not blame him."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Pi came late and Cao Wei did not reproach him."

sentences.zh: 邀一時之榮，忘委付之重，竊用恥焉，大王亦安用之哉！

translations.literal: To chase a moment's glory and forget the weight of commission—I am ashamed to do so; why would Your Majesty employ me!"
translations.idiomatic: To grasp a moment's gain and forget the charge given me—I would be ashamed; why would you want such a man!"

sentences.zh: 」熾磐乃遣武台手書喻政，政曰：「汝為國儲，不能盡節，面縛於人，棄父負君，虧萬世之業，賢政義士，豈如汝乎！

translations.literal: Chibpan sent Wutai's own hand to persuade Xianzheng; Xianzheng said: "You are the heir of the state and could not exhaust your integrity—bound face in hand to others, abandoning father and betraying lord, ruining the enterprise of ten thousand generations; I, Xianzheng the righteous man, am not like you!"
translations.idiomatic: Chibpan sent Wutai's own letter; Xianzheng answered: "You were heir of the realm yet could not die with honor—you bound yourself to the enemy, forsook your father, betrayed your lord, and ruined a thousand years of work. I, Xianzheng, am not such a man!"

sentences.zh: 」既而聞傉檀至左南，乃降。

translations.literal: Later hearing Rutan had reached Zuonan, he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Rutan had reached Zuonan, he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 熾磐以傉檀為驃騎大將軍，封左南公。

translations.literal: Chibpan made Rutan Grand General of Agile Cavalry and enfeoffed him as Duke of Zuonan.
translations.idiomatic: Chibpan made Rutan Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Zuonan.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，為熾磐所鴆。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was poisoned by Chibpan.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Chibpan poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 左右勸傉檀解藥，傉檀曰：「吾病豈宜療邪！

translations.literal: His attendants urged Rutan to take antidote; Rutan said: "My illness—how should it be cured!"
translations.idiomatic: Attendants pressed antidote on him; Rutan said: "This sickness—why cure it!"

sentences.zh: 」遂死，時年五十一，在位十三年，偽諡景王。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-one, having reigned thirteen years; his false posthumous title was King Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-one after thirteen years' reign, posthumously titled King Jing.

sentences.zh: 武台後亦為熾磐所殺。

translations.literal: Wutai later was also killed by Chibpan.
translations.idiomatic: Wutai was later killed by Chibpan as well.

sentences.zh: 傉檀少子保周、臘於破羌、俱延子覆龍、鹿孤孫副周、烏孤孫承缽皆奔沮渠蒙遜。

translations.literal: Rutan's young sons Baozhou and La, Juyan's son Fulong, Lilugu's grandson Fuzhou, and Wugu's grandson Chengbo all fled to Juqu Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan's sons Baozhou and La, Juyan's son Fulong, Lilugu's grandson Fuzhou, and Wugu's grandson Chengbo fled to Juqu Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 久之，歸魏，魏以保周為張掖王，覆龍酒泉公，破羌西平公，副周永平公，承缽昌松公。

translations.literal: Long afterward they returned to Wei; Wei made Baozhou Prince of Zhangye, Fulong Duke of Jiuquan, La Duke of Xiping, Fuzhou Duke of Yongping, and Chengbo Duke of Changsong.
translations.idiomatic: Years later they went to Wei; Wei made Baozhou Prince of Zhangye, Fulong Duke of Jiuquan, La Duke of Xiping, Fuzhou Duke of Yongping, and Chengbo Duke of Changsong.

sentences.zh: 烏孤以安帝隆安元年僭立，至傉檀三世，凡十九年，以安帝義熙十年滅。

translations.literal: From Wugu's presumptive founding in Long'an year 1 of Emperor An through Rutan's three generations, altogether nineteen years; destroyed in Yixi year 10 of Emperor An.
translations.idiomatic: From Wugu's founding in Long'an 1 of Emperor An through three generations to Rutan, the line lasted nineteen years; it perished in Yixi 10 of Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 【評贊】

translations.literal: Commentary and Praise
translations.idiomatic: Historian's Commentary and Eulogy

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：禿髮累葉酋豪，擅強邊服，控弦玉塞，躍馬金山，候滿月而窺兵，乘折膠而縱鏑，禮容弗被，聲教斯阻。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Tufa for generations were tribal chiefs, dominating the borderlands, drawing bows at Jade Pass and leaping horses at Golden Mountain; waiting for the full moon to spy on troops and riding the bent-bow season to loose arrows—civilized ritual did not reach them, royal teaching was thereby blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: For generations the Tufa were frontier chiefs who ruled the marches, strung bows at Jade Pass and rode at Golden Mountain, raided under the full moon and shot when the bow would bend—court ritual never touched them, imperial teaching never reached them.

sentences.zh: 烏孤納苻渾之策，治兵以討不賓；

translations.literal: Wugu adopted Fu Hun's plan to train troops and punish the unsubmissive;
translations.idiomatic: Wugu took Fu Hun's counsel, drilled troops, and punished rebels;

sentences.zh: 鹿孤從史暠之言，建學而延胄子。

translations.literal: Lilugu followed Shi Gao's counsel to establish schools and extend to the royal sons.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu heeded Shi Gao, founded schools, and taught the royal sons.

sentences.zh: 遂能開疆河右，抗衡強國。

translations.literal: Thus they could open territory in the lands west of the river and balance a strong state.
translations.idiomatic: So they opened lands west of the Yellow River and stood against great powers.

sentences.zh: 道由人弘，抑此之謂！

translations.literal: The Way is enlarged by men—is this not meant!
translations.idiomatic: The Way advances through men—so it was here!

sentences.zh: 傉檀承累捷之銳，藉二昆之資，摧呂氏算無遣策，取姑臧兵不血刃，武略雄圖，比蹤前烈。

translations.literal: Rutan inherited the edge of repeated victories and borrowed the resources of two elder brothers, smashed the Lü clan with schemes leaving nothing untried, took Guzang without blood on blades—martial design and heroic plan, matching traces of former exemplars.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan rode the momentum of repeated victories and his brothers' legacy, outschemed the Lü house, and took Guzang without drawing a blade—his martial vision matched the great kings of old.

sentences.zh: 既而叨竊重位，盈滿易期，窮兵以逞其心，縱慝自貽其弊，地奪于蒙遜，勢衄于赫連，覆國喪身，猶為幸也。

translations.literal: Then he usurped a heavy position; fullness easily brings its term; he exhausted troops to vent his heart and let wickedness invite its own harm; land was taken by Mengxun, momentum checked by Helian—ruined state and lost body, and even that was fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Then he clung to a throne too heavy for him; fullness invites ruin; he spent armies to feed his pride and wickedness to destroy himself—Mengxun seized his lands, Helian broke his power; to lose realm and life was still a mercy.

sentences.zh: 昔宋殤好戰，致災于華督；

translations.literal: In old times Duke Shang of Song loved war and brought disaster on Hua Du;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Duke Shang of Song loved war and brought Hua Du to ruin;

sentences.zh: 楚靈黷武，取殺於乾溪。

translations.literal: King Ling of Chu doted on arms and met killing at Ganxi.
translations.idiomatic: King Ling of Chu doted on arms and died at Ganxi.

sentences.zh: 異代同亡，其于傉檀見之矣。

translations.literal: Different ages, same ruin—for Rutan this is seen.
translations.idiomatic: Different ages, the same end—so it was with Rutan.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：禿髮弟兄，擅雄群虜。

translations.literal: Praise says: Tufa brothers dominated the barbarian hosts.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Tufa brothers ruled the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 開疆河外，清氛西土。

translations.literal: They opened territory beyond the river and cleared the air of the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: They carved a realm beyond the river and cleared the western sky.

sentences.zh: 傉檀傑出，騰駕時英。

translations.literal: Rutan stood out, vaulting over the heroes of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan rose above the heroes of his age.

sentences.zh: 窮兵黷武，喪國頹聲。

translations.literal: Exhausting troops and doting on war—ruined state and fallen fame.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his armies on war—realm lost, name in ruins.
